## CLAUDE  (2026-10-08 22:42:04 UTC)

**The fee rulebook** is the system's standing list of rules that decide, for every fee or cost on a loan, whether it is **integral to the EIR** (spread through the yield over the loan's life) or **period income** (recognised when earned, outside the EIR). IFRS 9 requires that split: B5.4.1 brings integral fees into the EIR; B5.4.2 excludes internal and holding costs; B5.4.3 lists origination and probable-drawdown commitment fees as integral. It lives in `database/seeders/EirAccountingRuleSeeder.php`, shows on the Governance Centre → Fee Classification screen, and is applied by `FeeRuleMatcher`.

**How it was determined** — by Dupleix, from the standard, not from MAIIC's practice. The dividing line in every rule is the one banks use:

- *Was the amount an unavoidable cost or price of putting the loan on the book?* → integral.
- *Is it the price of a service over time, or contingent on something that hadn't happened at origination?* → period income.

The 30 rules sit in priority bands, exclusions above inclusions, so a specific carve-out wins over a general rule:

| Band | Rules | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| 5–7 | E-Banker LOS agreement / legal / other fee charged at disbursement | integral |
| 10–16 | Internal admin and staff cost; recovery, enforcement and litigation legal; general legal; penalty and default charges | period income (excluded) |
| 20–34 | Arrangement, structuring, front-end fees; MAIIC GLs 4873 (arrangement received) and 4871 (legal received); origination legal; security perfection and stamp duty; valuation; broker commission; commitment fee where drawdown probable | integral |
| 40–56 | Monitoring, annual review, admin/ledger, prepayment, restructuring, syndication fees; insurance recharges; VAT and withholding | period income |
| 51 | **Keyman insurance premium — awaiting ruling** (open item O13) | period income provisionally |
| 96 | Any other levy | period income |

A rule matches on fee type, income GL, cash direction and a keyword in the description; a fee no rule recognises stays unclassified on purpose — silence is the correct output, and it's a question for a human.

**What it does to MAIIC's actual fees.** The 87 fees landed from E-Banker's charges table (P2_07) are all "Agreement fee (%)", "Legal fee (%)" or "Other fee (%)" charged at disbursement — 39, 38 and 10. I dry-ran the rulebook against them just now: all 87 would classify as integral under rules 5–7, none unmatched. Every one would go into the EIR.

**Why that hasn't happened.** The matcher only applies **approved** rules, and all 30 are unapproved: the rulebook is Dupleix's proposal and needs MAIIC's sign-off (Dr Thom, as the spec's section 4 lists it) before it classifies anything. That's the gate that leaves 20 solved EIRs unlocked — a contract can't lock its EIR while a fee on it is unreviewed. The ask of Dr Thom is therefore small and specific: confirm that the three E-Banker disbursement fees are integral (the standard answer), and rule on keyman insurance. That one approval unlocks 20 EIRs; the moratorium-type decision unlocks 51 schedules.

**Status update:** H10 is fixed and pushed (`4a98dca`): defaults from inception, migration applied to the demo copy, test on the earliest origination date, EIR coverage on the clean install 12 → 26 of 135, golden 9/9. The audit and the After Build Report (now with the coverage table in section 3) are re-rendered to OneDrive and docs/.

not held in the core system. At the EIR meeting on 24 September it was agreed that Credit would provide

2. Why offer letters, when we now have the system data
Since Monday we have received the full data dictionary of E-Banker and eighteen extracts from it, and we
can now tie the loan ledger to the trial balance to the cent. That settles what the system holds. It does not
settle what the contract says, and the effective interest rate (EIR) is calculated on the contract: the amount
approved, the rate and how it is built up, the fees deducted, and the repayment terms the customer signed
for.
The system record and the signed letter are not always the same. We have already found two of the ten
sample loans where the rate in the core differs from the rate typed on the letter (Ebenezer Midian 31% in
the core against 25.1% on the letter; JAT Group 33% against 25.3%), and two take-on loans where the
approved amount in the system looks mis-keyed. Only the signed letter can say which is right. That is why
we ask for the letters themselves.
What "signed offer letter" means here: the final version accepted and signed by the customer, with
every schedule and annex, as kept on the credit file. A draft or system-generated letter is useful but is
not the contract. The ten letters we received on 17 September appear to be the unsigned issue
versions; if any of them is in fact the signed version, please just say so and we will not ask again for
that one.

3. Group A: the signed letters for the ten sample loans, as agreed on 24 September

charts Barry provided, whose interest we rebuilt from the ledger, and which the walkthrough followed from
approval to posting. The reason the signed letter is needed for each is the same reason it was asked for in
September: the fees deducted at drawdown and the margin over the reference rate are the two terms that
make an effective interest rate differ from the rate on the system, and neither is held in the core. From each
signed letter we will read:

the approved amount and the drawdown terms (single or in tranches);

the interest rate, and how it is made up: the reference rate, the spread above it (the margin), and
whether the rate is fixed or moves with the Reserve Bank rate;

the fees: arrangement, legal, insurance and any other charge deducted from the advance, with the
amount or percentage;

the repayment terms: frequency, first instalment date, tenor, and any moratorium on principal or on
interest;

the signature date, which fixes the contract date for the EIR.

--- content ---
"""Render selected pages of the scanned offer letters to PNG for reading."""
import sys, os, glob
import pypdfium2 as pdfium

SRC = r"C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\Offer Letters\Signed Offer Letter - Received 7 october"
OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "letters")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

def render(name_fragment, pages=None, scale=1.3):
    f = [p for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(SRC, "*.pdf")) if name_fragment.lower() in os.path.basename(p).lower()]
    assert len(f) == 1, (name_fragment, f)
    pdf = pdfium.PdfDocument(f[0])
    n = len(pdf)
    pages = pages or list(range(1, n + 1))
    out = []
    for p in pages:
        if p == -1: p = n
        if p < 1 or p > n: continue
        img = pdf[p - 1].render(scale=scale).to_pil()
        path = os.path.join(OUT, f"{name_fragment.replace(' ', '_')}_p{p:02}.png")
        img.save(path, optimize=True)
        out.append(path)
    print(name_fragment, "pages", n, "->", [os.path.basename(x) for x in out])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    frag = sys.argv[1]
    pages = [int(x) for x in sys.argv[2].split(",")] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    scale = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 1.3
    render(frag, pages, scale)

````

## 1. In one paragraph

Credit sent what was asked for, and more than the unsigned issue versions of 17 September ever could: real contracts, signed by the borrower and by MAIIC's Acting CEO and Head of Legal, with the rate build-up, the itemised charges, the application of funds, the moratorium and the repayment terms written in. All twelve letters requested are present (both Group B letters included), and they settle the four questions the system could not: how each rate is built (reference rate plus margin, and which reference), what the fees were and the fact that they were **financed into the loan** rather than deducted from cash, the moratorium type and length, and the two sanction amounts. Three of the thirteen are for a different facility or vintage from the account the request named (JVD, Mphunzitsi, the second Mchinji file), so three follow-up letters are still needed. For the engine, the single most useful fact is the first: every letter's Application of Funds shows the borrower receiving the loan less the charges, with the facility booked at the charge-inclusive amount, which is exactly what the EIR must be solved on.

## 4. What the letters settle

1. **The sanction questions (Group B).** Mchinji: the facility was 100,000,000, disbursed in two tranches of 50,000,000; the system's 50,000,000 is one tranche and the 31 July 2024 opening balance of 100,000,000 is the full facility. VNC: the facility was 200,000,000; the system's 20,000,000 is a typing slip. Barry can correct both sanction amounts in the loan master against these letters.
2. **The fees, and how they were taken.** Every letter's Application of Funds shows the loan amount, the charges, and a total equal to the facility: the charges were financed into the principal and the borrower received the difference. The system books the facility at the charge-inclusive total (it agrees to the kwacha on all eight matched loans), and E-Banker's charges table (P2_07) carries the same figures for the four FInES and MAIIC Industrial loans (Ebenezer, Gojet, JAT, Microloan). For the five term loans on GL 1050401 (Lake Malawi, Police SACCO, Milele, Mphunzitsi, Promenade) **P2_07 holds no fees at all**; the letters are the only record, and the amounts must be keyed from them. For the EIR this is the central fact: the initial net investment is the facility less the charges (300,000,000 on Ebenezer's 314,900,900), and every charge on every letter is an origination charge of the kind the fee rulebook classifies as integral (arrangement, legal, stamp duty, levy). The rulebook's rules 5 to 7 and 20 to 26 cover all of them; nothing on these letters is period income.
3. **The rate build-up.** Three patterns, by product: FInES loans at a fixed 10 percent; MAIIC Industrial loans at the reference lending rate (25.3 percent in 2025) plus a margin of 5.9 to 8 percent; term loans on 1050401 at a **Treasury-note rate plus a small margin** (2-year 28.75% + 6; 5-year 32% + 2.45 or 2.75; 7-year + 0.75). The margins the system lacks are now known for all twelve. Two consequences for the engine: (a) the spread derivation (step 5g) measures every loan against PLR, and for the term loans the reference is a Treasury note, so their derived "spread" is not the contractual margin; (b) the system records the term loans as FIXED, but every letter says the rate is "subject to variation at MAIIC's discretion" and is expressed as note plus margin, so under the `rate_change_classification` setting they are floating in substance. The September "25.1% against 31%" and "25.3% against 33%" differences are explained: the LOS print showed the reference rate, the letter shows reference plus margin, and the core's 31% and 33% were right.
4. **Moratoria.** The letters state the type in words: JVD "12 months (Principal and Interest)", Lake Malawi "9 months (principal plus interest)", Ebenezer "No moratorium required", Milele "None". That is the field E-Banker leaves blank on 51 contracts and the reason the schedule generator refuses them. For the sample, the system is wrong on two (Lake Malawi 0 against 9; Promenade 0 against an unlabelled six months between payout and first instalment, which is why the ledger shows no interest for two months and then a catch-up) and models Gojet's semi-annual frequency as a 6-month moratorium (same cash flows, different label). The scheme rule Barry proposed ("Principle Only" as E-Banker's default) is contradicted by the two letters that state a moratorium: both are principal **and** interest, capitalising.
5. **Repayment frequency and tranches.** Monthly, quarterly (JAT), semi-annual (Gojet, Microloan) and annual (Milele) instalments all occur; Milele and Lake Malawi disburse in tranches under a schedule; Mchinji is a revolving line. The schedule generator handles the first three; annual instalments and tranche schedules need the letter's schedule keyed, since the core holds neither.

| Mphunzitsi: the letter is 1,047,653,000 of July 2025; the account is 1,560,150,000 of August 2026 with the same 30,000,000 arrangement fee | Either a top-up or a mis-keyed sanction; the fee matches the 2025 letter, which suggests the sanction, not the fee, is what changed | The variation or top-up letter for account 106050000014, or confirmation that 1,560,150,000 is a keying error |

| Term-loan fees not in P2_07 | Five of the twelve loans' fees exist only on paper | Tamanda's take-on fee template, extended to the 1050401 loans, keyed from the letters |

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-08 23:04:13 UTC)

No — it's the same mechanism on every letter; I phrased it badly. Only the headline figure differs by vintage.

**What actually happens, on all twelve:** MAIIC pays the arrangement and legal fees out of the loan proceeds on the borrower's behalf, and the borrower owes them as part of the principal. VNC's 2022 letter says it in words: *"Legal fees — to be paid upfront by MAIIC on behalf of the Borrower from the proceeds of the loan"*, with Loan 200,000,000 + legal 3,282,500 + arrangement 3,000,000 = **Total 206,282,500**.

So in every case:

- **Cash the borrower actually receives** = the "Loan" line (Ebenezer 300,000,000; VNC 200,000,000).
- **Principal the borrower owes, and on which interest is charged** = Loan + charges (Ebenezer 314,900,900; VNC 206,282,500).

The only difference is which number is in the heading. The 2025–26 letters headline the fee-inclusive total ("Term loan for MWK 314,900,900"); the 2022–23 letters headline the cash amount ("Term loan for MWK 200,000,000") and show the fee-inclusive total further down. Same economics, different presentation.

"Netted against the disbursement" and "added to the loan" are therefore both true at once, and that is precisely the IFRS 9 case: the fee is an integral origination charge, the initial net investment is the cash that left MAIIC (300m), and the contractual cash flows repay 314.9m plus interest at 31.2% — so the effective rate solves above 31.2%. The engine already does this correctly if the fee is classified integral: `EirContractInputService` takes the drawn amount less reviewed integral fees. What it must *not* do is treat 314.9m as the cash out, which is what happens today while the rulebook is unapproved and the fees sit unclassified.

One extra point from that VNC page: it carries a **6-month moratorium on capital and interest** (payout Oct 2022, first repayment Apr 2023) where the system holds 0 — so three of the twelve letters now state a principal-and-interest moratorium, none a principal-only one. I'll correct the wording in the review memo and the memory note.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-08 23:09:22 UTC)

Honest rating, by layer, against what spec v4 asks for and what a CFO needs before relying on a number. Scale: 0–10 where 10 = complete, proven, and safe to sign off.

| Layer | Rating | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Data foundation** (landing zone, gates, versioning, build methods A/B/C, ledger as record, take-on landing, bootstrap) | **8.5** | Proven to the cent on 2,361 account-months and the December 2025 GL. Gaps: trial balances bypass the landing zone, several gates not at the door, 300/401 counted as cash. |
| **Governance** (48 settings, maker-checker, effective dating, audit trail, lock) | **7** | Built and enforced server-side; but the lock is honoured by only one writer, thresholds sit outside maker-checker, the admin role bypasses the two-person rule, and 14 settings are read by nothing yet. |
| **EIR / revenue recognition** | **5** | The solver, lock and schedule generator are sound. But coverage is 26 of 135 loans (fee rulebook and moratorium type pending), Stage 3 net interest doesn't take effect, the roll-forward deducts schedule cash after a borrower stops paying, tranche drawdowns aren't in the vector, and the term-loan reference rate is wrong (PLR vs Treasury notes). |
| **Impairment (ECL)** | **3.5** | Runs end-to-end on all loans, but on the wrong basis: 12-month PD for Stage 2, undiscounted, tenor units inconsistent, LGD workout flawed, scenario weighting applied twice, reports split by the wrong stage. The 8.94bn cannot be quoted. |
| **Forward-looking and scenarios** | **5.5** | Chain, guardrail, fits, governed sets and lineage exist; but the bootstrap self-approves the fit, no overlay register, no screen to set weights, sensitivity disagrees with the route. |
| **Regulatory (RBM)** | **7** | Classification, provisioning and the provisional return are now on the Gazette's bands with tests; the prescribed form and restructure data are external. |
| **Mega Farm** | **3** | Mechanics run but misread D30; nothing of section 16 beyond staging and PD. Blocked on MAIIC anyway. |
| **UI, help, dark mode, navigation** | **8.5** | Suite shell, 120 screens themed and proven, help re-worded. Two spec screens still CLI-only. |
| **Security of the platform as deployed** | **2** | 180 legacy routes without a login and one SQL interpolation. Everything built in this engagement is guarded; the fork is not. |
| **Testing and proof** | **6.5** | 455 passing tests, bootstrap from nothing, golden ties — but several engine tests assert the wrong behaviour, and 92 legacy tests fail. |

**Overall: about 5.5 out of 10 — roughly 60% of spec v4 by requirement count, but less than that by weight**, because the two things a CFO signs (the ECL and the revenue line) are the two layers furthest from done. It is a genuinely strong *data and governance platform* wrapped around an *impairment engine that is not yet IFRS 9* and sitting on a *product fork that is not yet safe to expose*.

What closes the gap, in order: a day for the legacy authentication; about two weeks of engine work (the audit's steps 2–7) to put the ECL and revenue on the right basis; then the spec gaps that depend on MAIIC's decisions (fee rulebook, moratorium type, D30, scenario weights, the RBM form). With those, I'd expect the data, governance and EIR layers at 9, impairment at 8, and the whole at a level MAIIC can put a number on.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-08 23:10:53 UTC)

From section 9 ("Order of work") of the audit — step 1 is the legacy authentication; these are the engine steps:

**2. Stage 2 lifetime PD, one tenor unit, Stage 3 from the reporting date, discounted LGD** (findings C1, C2, C3, H7) — 3 to 4 days.
Stage 2 provided on the lifetime PD instead of the 12-month PD; `remaining_tenor` stored and read in one unit (months); Stage 3 loss measured at the reporting date with recoveries discounted from their own dates; the cohort LGD discounted and no longer counting a written-off loan as recovered. A worked example per stage in the tests, and the FS note re-run.

**3. Stage 3 allowance into the revenue engine; revenue after ECL; schedule fallback bounded by the feed** (C5, C6) — 2 days.
The revenue engine reads the allowance the engine actually writes (`ecl_value`) so Stage 3 interest is on the net carrying amount; the bootstrap runs the ECL before the revenue step; the roll-forward stops deducting scheduled instalments as cash once the ledger shows no receipt. The revenue-shift golden number is born here, so Dr Thom's first approved run follows this step.

**4. Write-offs (300) and equity entries (401) out of cash** (H1) — a day plus the re-proof.
A write-off reduces gross carrying through the allowance; the Nascomex 401 entries are excluded from loan cash; the ledger ties re-run with the exceptions stated.

**5. Bootstrap to the spec's rule on fits and approvals; one scenario weighting; sensitivity from the per-scenario ECL** (C9, H3, M8) — 2 days.
The bootstrap applies the route with the overlay at zero instead of approving a fit itself; one governed scenario set weighted once (not the route *and* the time-phased engine each weighting); the sensitivity and the disclosure read the same per-scenario ECLs; the bootstrap stops giving fee-review and EIR-lock approvals under its label.

**6. Thresholds at the period end under maker-checker; the lock honoured by every writer; admin override governed** (H11, H4, H9) — 1.5 days.
Staging thresholds resolved as at the period end, not today, and proposed/approved like any setting; one lock check called by every engine that writes to a period; the admin bypass of maker-checker made a governed setting or removed. (H10, governance dating, was in this step and is done.)

**7. Tranche drawdowns in the EIR vector; PD annualisation; post-stage splits; gross carrying in the note** (H2, H8, H5, H6) — 3 days.
Later drawdowns enter the cash-flow vector at their dates from P3_12; a 12-month PD from a short window annualised; every report splits by the post-qualitative stage the ECL was measured on; the FS note's gross carrying amount is the carrying amount, not the EAD.

Roughly 12–13 engineer-days in all. Steps 2 and 3 are the ones that change the two numbers the CFO signs.

<?php

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpException;

/**
 * Every web route needs a login unless it is on the public list below.
 *
 * System audit of 9 October 2026, finding C7: 180 routes of the product the
 * platform was forked from (loan-book import, collateral, the transition
 * matrix and LGD writes into the loan book, the ECL recalculation, the legacy
 * regression approval, the macro and scenario CRUD) had no auth middleware in
 * the route file or the controller. Rather than touch each of them, this one
 * gate runs in the web group after the session starts: a guest is sent to
 * the login page (or gets 401 on a JSON request), and the legacy financial
 * modules also require the suite permission they belong to, by URI prefix.
 * A route that declares its own, stricter permission keeps it.
 */
class RequireLogin
{
    /** Route names, or name prefixes ending in '*', that need no login. */
    public const PUBLIC_ROUTES = [
        'login', 'logout', 'register', 'password.*', 'two-factor.*', 'verification.*',
        'terms.show', 'policy.show', 'captcha', 'captcha.*', 'ebanker-feed.api',
        'sanctum.csrf-cookie', 'livewire.*', 'ignition.*',
    ];

    /** URIs (first segment or full path pattern) that need no login. */
    public const PUBLIC_URIS = [
        '/', 'login', 'logout', 'register', 'captcha', 'forgot-password', 'reset-password', 'reset-password/*',
        'two-factor-challenge', 'email/verify/*', 'email/verification-notification', 'user/confirm-password',
        'privacy-policy', 'terms-of-service', 'broadcasting/auth', 'websockets', 'websockets/*', 'livewire/*',
        'sanctum/csrf-cookie', 'api/ebanker-feed/pack', '_ignition/*', 'cache',
    ];

    /**
     * Legacy financial modules and the suite permission they belong to. The
     * first matching prefix wins; a module absent from the list is gated by
     * the login alone.
     */
    public const MODULE_PERMISSIONS = [
        'loan_application' => 'loans',
        'loan-books' => 'loans',
        'save-loan-book' => 'loans',
        'contracts' => 'loans',
        'groups' => 'loans',
        'collateral' => 'loans',
        'transition-matrix' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'transition-matrix-cummulative' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'transition-profile' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'transition-profiles' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'loss-given-default' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'lgd-calculations' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'lgd-payment-report' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'expected-credit-loss' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'credit-loss-data' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'regression' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'macro-statistics' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'macro-forecast-weighted' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'scenarios' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'scenario-profiles' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'external-calculations' => 'reports.ifrs9',
        'file' => 'loans',
        'communication' => 'settings',
        'docs' => 'manual.view',
    ];

    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next)
    {
        if ($this->isPublic($request)) {
            return $next($request);
        }

        if (! Auth::check()) {
            if ($request->expectsJson()) {
                throw new HttpException(401, 'Login required.');
            }
            return redirect()->guest(route('login'));
        }

        $permission = $this->modulePermission($request);
        if ($permission !== null && ! Auth::user()->can($permission)) {
            throw new HttpException(403, "User does not have the right permissions ({$permission}).");
        }

        return $next($request);
    }

    private function isPublic(Request $request): bool
    {
        $name = (string) optional($request->route())->getName();
        foreach (self::PUBLIC_ROUTES as $pattern) {
            if ($name !== '' && ($pattern === $name || (str_ends_with($pattern, '*') && str_starts_with($name, rtrim($pattern, '*'))))) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        foreach (self::PUBLIC_URIS as $uri) {
            if ($request->is($uri)) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }

    private function modulePermission(Request $request): ?string
    {
        $first = explode('/', trim($request->path(), '/'))[0] ?? '';
        if ($first === 'api') {
            $first = explode('/', trim($request->path(), '/'))[1] ?? '';
        }

        return self::MODULE_PERMISSIONS[$first] ?? null;
    }
}

        $query = "UPDATE transition_profile_options SET ordering_index = CASE id ";
        $ids = [];

        foreach ($startCategories as $index => $category) {
            $query .= "WHEN {$category['id']} THEN " . ($index + 1) . " ";
            $ids[] = $category['id'];
        }

        foreach ($endCategories as $index => $category) {
            $query .= "WHEN {$category['id']} THEN " . ($index + 1) . " ";
            $ids[] = $category['id'];
        }
        
        $query .= "END WHERE id IN (" . implode(',', $ids) . ")";
    
        DB::statement($query);
    
        return redirect()->route('transition-profiles.config', $profileId)->with('message', 'Categories sorted successfully');
    }

<?php

namespace Tests\Feature\Security;

use App\Http\Middleware\RequireLogin;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use Tests\TestCase;

/**
 * System audit of 9 October 2026, finding C7: every web route needs a login
 * unless it is on the public list, and the legacy financial modules need
 * the suite permission they belong to.
 */
class RequireLoginTest extends TestCase
{
    protected $seed = false;

    /** Every GET web route refuses a guest: a redirect to login (or 401/404 for parameterised routes), never 200. */
    public function test_no_get_route_answers_a_guest_with_a_page(): void
    {
        $answered = [];
        foreach (Route::getRoutes() as $route) {
            if (! in_array('GET', $route->methods(), true) || ! in_array('web', $route->gatherMiddleware(), true)) {
                continue;
            }
            $uri = '/' . ltrim($route->uri(), '/');
            if (str_contains($uri, '{')) {
                continue; // needs a model; the gate runs before binding, so these behave as the un-parameterised ones
            }
            $public = $this->isPublic($route->getName(), $route->uri());
            $response = $this->get($uri);
            if (! $public && $response->getStatusCode() === 200) {
                $answered[] = $uri;
            }
        }
        $this->assertSame([], $answered, 'Routes that served a page to a guest: ' . implode(', ', $answered));
    }

    public function test_a_guest_is_sent_to_the_login_page_from_a_legacy_module(): void
    {
        $this->get('/collateral/register/list')->assertRedirect(route('login'));
        $this->get('/expected-credit-loss/list')->assertRedirect(route('login'));
        $this->getJson('/api/get-tables')->assertStatus(401);
    }

    public function test_the_public_routes_still_answer(): void
    {
        $this->get('/login')->assertStatus(200);
    }

    private function isPublic(?string $name, string $uri): bool
    {
        foreach (RequireLogin::PUBLIC_ROUTES as $p) {
            if ($name !== null && ($p === $name || (str_ends_with($p, '*') && str_starts_with($name, rtrim($p, '*'))))) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        foreach (RequireLogin::PUBLIC_URIS as $u) {
            if (fnmatch($u, $uri) || $u === $uri) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }
}

````

    private function projectionMonths(object $loan,string $id,CarbonImmutable $asOf,int $stage,Collection $recoveries): int
    {
        $last=DB::table('contract_cashflow_schedule')->where('contract_id',$id)->where('schedule_version',1)->whereDate('due_date','>',$asOf)->max('due_date');
        if($stage===3 && $recoveries->isNotEmpty()) $last=$recoveries->max('recovery_date');
        $months=$last?max(1,$asOf->diffInMonths(CarbonImmutable::parse($last)->endOfMonth())):(int)ceil((float)($loan->remaining_tenor??0)*12);
        if($months<1)throw new RuntimeException('A remaining contractual horizon is unavailable.');
        return $stage===1?min(12,$months):min(600,$months);
    }

    private function horizonYears(object $loan, string $reportingPeriod): ?float
    {
        $remaining = (float) ($loan->remaining_tenor ?? 0);
        if ($remaining <= 0 && ! empty($loan->due_date)) {
            $asOf = CarbonImmutable::createFromFormat('Y-m-d', $this->rates->periodKey($reportingPeriod) . '-01')->endOfMonth();
            $due = CarbonImmutable::parse($loan->due_date);
            $remaining = $due->greaterThan($asOf) ? $asOf->diffInDays($due) / 365 : 0.0;
        }
        if ($remaining <= 0) return null;

        $stage = (int) ($loan->calculated_ifrs9_stage
            ?? $loan->ifrs9stage_post_qualitative
            ?? $loan->ifrs9stage_pre_qualitative
            ?? $loan->ifrs9_stage
            ?? 0);

        return round($stage === 1 ? min(1.0, $remaining) : $remaining, 8);
    }
}

        // The engines use POWER() in SQL (lifetime PD from the 12-month PD over

description: Commit step 2
--- command ---
cd /c/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9 && git add app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php app/Http/Controllers/ExpectedCreditLossController.php app/Services/Pd/PdEngineService.php app/Http/Controllers/TransitionMatrixController.php app/Services/Ecl/TimePhasedEclService.php app/Services/Ecl/EclDiscountingService.php app/Jobs/ProcessLoanImportJob.php app/Imports/LoanBooksImport.php app/Services/Lgd/LgdEngineService.php app/Models/LossGivenDefault.php tests/Feature/Ecl tests/Feature/Pd && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
ECL on the IFRS 9 basis by stage: lifetime PD for Stage 2, one tenor unit, Stage 3 at the reporting date, discounted LGD (audit C1, C2, C3, H7, M3)

C1: the allowance was 12-month PD x LGD x EAD for every stage; lifetime_pd was written and never read. The ECL update now measures by the post-qualitative stage: Stage 1 over the shorter of twelve months and the remaining life, Stage 2 over the lifetime, 1 - (1 - PD12)^(months/12), Stage 3 at 1. A Stage 2 loan with 36 months to run and a 10 percent PD is provided at 27.1 percent, not 10. POWER() is registered on sqlite so the tests run the engine's own SQL.

C2: remaining_tenor was months from the governed build and years from the legacy importers, read as months by one engine and years by three. It is months everywhere: the PD engine, the Monthly Probability screen, the time-phased engine, the discounting service and both legacy importers; the lifetime floor is one month, not one year (M3).

C3: the time-phased engine projected a Stage 3 loss along the contractual schedule and discounted it from the last due date (60,000 became 49,587), and netted a recovery plan before discounting. The loss is now measured at the reporting date; with a plan it is EAD less the present value of each recovery from its own date, written as EAD and negative recovery rows. The test that asserted the understated range asserts the IFRS 9 figure.

H7: the LGD cohort workout read a loan absent from the end book as fully recovered and counted a cured loan in the recovery denominator. Cure and recovery are exclusive; recovery is the cash received over the window (the loan book's cumulative repayments, month by month) discounted at the loan's locked EIR or contractual rate; a loan absent from the end book is a write-off unless its last row shows it settled. written_offs and the discounted recovery are recorded on the run.

Clean install at August 2026: ECL 10.23bn (Stage 1 1.64bn, Stage 2 3.40bn, Stage 3 5.18bn) against 8.94bn before; cohort LGD 59.06 percent discounted; golden checks 9 of 9.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log -1 --format='%h %s'

"""    /**
     * The loss allowance the net basis nets off (IFRS 9 5.4.1(b)): the
     * allowance in the books at the start of the month, which is the ECL the
     * engine wrote on the prior month's loan-book row. The current month's
     * ECL stands in when the prior month has none; the legacy
     * expected_loss_provision column, which only a legacy importer fills, is
     * the last resort. System audit of 9 October 2026, finding C6: the engine
     * read only that column, nothing in the governed chain wrote it, and
     * Stage 3 interest accrued on gross while the setting said net.
     */
    private function openingAllowance(string $contractId, string $period, object $loan): float
    {
        $prior = CarbonImmutable::createFromFormat('Y-m-d', $period . '-01')->subMonth()->format('Y-m');
        $previous = $this->loanSnapshot($contractId, $prior);
        foreach ([$previous->ecl_value ?? null, $loan->ecl_value ?? null, $loan->expected_loss_provision ?? null] as $candidate) {
            if ($candidate !== null) {
                return max(0.0, (float) $candidate);
            }
        }

        return 0.0;
    }

    private function loanSnapshot(string $contractId, string $period): ?object
    {"""),
# C5: the schedule stands in only outside the feed's coverage
("""        $window = DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->where('contract_id', $contractId)
            ->selectRaw('MIN(transaction_date) as first_txn, MAX(transaction_date) as last_txn')->first();
        $covered = $window && $window->first_txn && $window->last_txn
            && $start->toDateString() <= substr((string) $window->last_txn, 0, 10)
            && $end->toDateString() >= substr((string) $window->first_txn, 0, 10);
""",
"""        // The ledger covers a month when the feed's postings run past its
        // start and the contract existed by its end; a covered month with no
        // receipt is zero cash, not the schedule. System audit of 9 October
        // 2026, finding C5: the window was the contract's own first and last
        // posting, so every month after a borrower's last receipt fell back to
        // the schedule and the roll-forward retired a loan nobody was paying.
        static $feedLast = null;
        $feedLast = $feedLast ?? (DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->max('transaction_date') ?? '');
        $window = DB::table('eir_actual_transactions')->where('contract_id', $contractId)
            ->selectRaw('MIN(transaction_date) as first_txn')->first();
        $contractStart = $window && $window->first_txn ? substr((string) $window->first_txn, 0, 10) : null;
        $covered = $feedLast !== '' && $contractStart !== null
            && $start->toDateString() <= substr((string) $feedLast, 0, 10)
            && $end->toDateString() >= $contractStart;
"""),
])

Stage 3 interest nets the allowance the engine wrote; schedule cash only outside the feed; ECL for every month (audit C5, C6, M17)

C6: the revenue engine netted loan_books.expected_loss_provision, which only a legacy importer fills, so the "net carrying amount" basis never took effect and Stage 3 interest accrued on gross. It now nets the opening allowance: the ECL the engine wrote on the prior month's loan-book row (the current month's when the prior has none; the legacy column last). The bootstrap runs the PD, the LGD and the pre-FLI ECL for every period before the revenue step (25 of 26 months on the clean install; July 2024 has no transition window), which is also the spec's "every period from the first full month" (M17).

C5: the cash window was the contract's own first and last posting, so every month after a borrower's last receipt fell back to the contractual schedule and the roll-forward retired a loan nobody was paying. The ledger now covers a month when the feed's postings run past its start and the contract existed by its end; a covered month without a receipt is zero cash. Schedule-derived months fell from most of the Stage 3 history to 3 of 483.

Clean install, August 2026, the nine locked Stage 3 contracts: allowance netted 1.00bn, interest 17.3m on the net amount, unwind 21.9m disclosed. Golden checks 9 of 9; bootstrap 120 s.

EOF

    public function test_a_write_off_reduces_the_gross_but_is_not_cash(): void
    {
        $this->seedLocked();
        $this->loan('C-1', '2025-01', 3);
        $this->actual('C-1', '2025-01-10', 'Principal+Interest', 100);
        $this->actual('C-1', '2025-01-20', 'Write-off', 300);
        $this->actual('C-1', '2025-01-25', 'Settlement in kind', 200);

        $result = (new EirRevenueService())->run('C-1', '2025-01');
        $row = DB::table('eir_amortisation')->first();

        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(100, $row->cash_received, 0.01);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(-500, $row->modification_gain_loss, 0.01);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta($row->opening_gross + $row->interest_accrued + $row->unwind_amount - 100 - 500, $row->closing_gross, 0.01);
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta(0, $result['unclassified_cash'], 0.01);
    }

Write-offs and settlements in kind leave the gross without being cash (audit H1, M15)

Type 300 (write-off) and 401 (the Nascomex loan settled by redemption of its preference shares) were in the receipt list, so they counted as cash received in the loan book's repayments and the EIR roll-forward. Spec 3.3 names 300 a write-off and 400/401 the equity entries. They are their own kinds now: in the balance (the carrying amount still uses every posting, so the ledger ties are unchanged at 9 of 9) but never in repayments; the EIR inputs carry them as 'Write-off' and 'Settlement in kind'; the revenue engine takes them off the gross as derecognition, disclosed on the row, not as cash. The 401 postings turn out to sit on GL 3065, which the ledger reader already excludes, so only the two write-offs (22.3m) were ever counted; the list was wrong all the same.

The 'Interest' entry leaves COLLECTION_TYPES as spec 7.4 says: an interest charge is not cash collected (M15). The revenue tests use the ledger path's own cash type.

    private function scenariosFor(object $loan,float $basePd,Collection $legacy): Collection

The bootstrap approves no fit and reviews no fee; one scenario weighting; the sensitivity reconciles to the allowance (audit C9, H3, M8, M9)

C9: the bootstrap proposed and approved the best regression fit under its own label and computed the ECL on it. Spec 6.10.1 step 6: on a clean install no fit is approved, the overlay is zero and the PD holds until two people approve a fit on the FLI Adjustments screen. The route now runs that way ("no approved fit for the period: manual overlay at zero, the PD holds"), and the label that bypasses the different-person rule on fit and set approval is the bootstrap's own constant, not any string.

M8: the bootstrap reviewed fee classifications under its label; Fee Classification is a Governance Centre screen and the review is a person's. The rulebook suggests only, and suggests nothing until MAIIC approves it.

H3: the time-phased engine weighted a second scenario set (the seeded ecl_scenario_assumptions) on top of the route's weighted PD. It now takes the governed set written on each loan by the route (per-scenario PD, the set's weights, LGD and EAD unshocked) and falls back to the legacy table only when no loan carries one. The last ECL of the bootstrap runs discounted through it where a locked EIR exists (21 loans on the clean install).

H3, M9: the sensitivity computed its own per-scenario ECL from typed multipliers on the stored ead column at 100 percent utilisation, so it never agreed with the allowance (10.24bn beside 8.94bn in the After Build Report). It now scales each loan's booked ECL by the ratio of stage PDs (lifetime for Stage 2, 1 for Stage 3) under the scenario's PD, from the route's per-scenario PD when the chain has run for the set, else the typed multiplier, and says which. The base scenario equals the booked allowance to the kwacha (9,509,808,295 on the clean install); the weighted figure is 9.88bn.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

--- content ---
<?php

namespace App\Support;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;
use RuntimeException;

/**
 * The one lock check every engine calls before it writes a period.
 *
 * A locked reporting period is never restated (spec 6.6, D21). Until the
 * system audit of 9 October 2026 (finding H4) only the loan-book build read
 * reporting_period_locks; the revenue roll-forward, the ECL, staging, the PD,
 * the LGD and the forward-looking route wrote freely into a locked month.
 */
final class ReportingPeriodLock
{
    public static function isLocked(string $period): bool
    {
        $period = self::normalise($period);
        if (! Schema::hasTable('reporting_period_locks')) {
            return false;
        }

        return DB::table('reporting_period_locks')->where('reporting_period', $period)->exists();
    }

    /** @throws LockedPeriodException */
    public static function assertOpen(string $period, string $what): void
    {
        if (self::isLocked($period)) {
            throw new LockedPeriodException(self::normalise($period), $what);
        }
    }

    private static function normalise(string $period): string
    {
        $digits = preg_replace('/\D/', '', $period);

        return strlen($digits) >= 6 ? substr($digits, 0, 4) . '-' . substr($digits, 4, 2) : $period;
    }
}

final class LockedPeriodException extends RuntimeException
{
    public function __construct(public readonly string $period, string $what)
    {
        parent::__construct("Reporting period {$period} is locked: {$what} cannot be written. A locked period is never restated; unlock it with a reason (eir:lock-period --unlock) if the restatement is deliberate.");
    }
}

````

--- content ---
<?php

namespace Tests\Feature\Eir;

use App\Services\Eir\EirRevenueService;
use App\Services\Eir\StagingService;
use App\Services\Fli\FliRouteService;
use App\Services\Lgd\LgdEngineService;
use App\Services\Pd\PdEngineService;
use App\Support\LockedPeriodException;
use App\Support\ReportingPeriodLock;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;
use Tests\TestCase;

/**
 * System audit of 9 October 2026, finding H4: a locked reporting period is
 * never restated, by any engine. Before, only the loan-book build read the
 * lock table.
 */
class ReportingPeriodLockTest extends TestCase
{
    protected $seed = false;

    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        parent::setUp();
        config(['database.default' => 'sqlite', 'database.connections.sqlite.database' => ':memory:']);
        DB::purge('sqlite'); DB::reconnect('sqlite');
        Schema::create('reporting_period_locks', function (Blueprint $t) { $t->increments('id'); $t->string('reporting_period'); $t->timestamps(); });
        DB::table('reporting_period_locks')->insert(['reporting_period' => '2025-12', 'created_at' => now(), 'updated_at' => now()]);
    }

    public function test_the_lock_is_read_in_any_period_spelling(): void
    {
        $this->assertTrue(ReportingPeriodLock::isLocked('2025-12'));
        $this->assertTrue(ReportingPeriodLock::isLocked('202512'));
        $this->assertTrue(ReportingPeriodLock::isLocked('2025-12-31'));
        $this->assertFalse(ReportingPeriodLock::isLocked('2026-01'));
    }

    public function test_every_engine_refuses_a_locked_period_before_touching_a_table(): void
    {
        foreach ([
            'PD' => fn () => (new PdEngineService())->run('2025-12', 1),
            'LGD' => fn () => (new LgdEngineService())->run('2025-12', 1),
            'FLI route' => fn () => app(FliRouteService::class)->apply('2025-12'),
            'staging' => fn () => app(StagingService::class)->stage('2025-12'),
        ] as $name => $call) {
            try {
                $call();
                $this->fail("{$name} wrote into a locked period");
            } catch (LockedPeriodException $e) {
                $this->assertSame('2025-12', $e->period, $name);
                $this->assertStringContainsString('never restated', $e->getMessage());
            }
        }
    }

    public function test_the_revenue_engine_reports_a_locked_period_as_blocked(): void
    {
        $result = (new EirRevenueService())->run('C-1', '2025-12', true, 1, 'a reason');

        $this->assertSame('BLOCKED', $result['status']);
        $this->assertStringContainsString('locked', $result['error']);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Services\Stress;

use App\Services\AuditLoggerService;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

/**
 * Stress testing as a service (spec v4 section 6.10.1, step 11): the
 * loan-level stress of the Stress Testing screen, lifted as it is so the
 * bootstrap and the scheduler can run it, and run for every scenario of
 * the approved set with the scenario's PD multiplier.
 */
class StressTestService
{
    public const EAD = '(COALESCE(carrying_amount,0) + COALESCE(commitments,0) * COALESCE(facility_utilisation_rate,1))';
    public const PD = 'COALESCE(pd_post_fli, pd_prefli, 0)';
    public const LGD = 'COALESCE(lgd_value, 0)';

    public function execute(string $period, ?int $portfolioId, array $pd, array $lg): array
    {
        // Per-stage CASE expressions (bindings in stage order 1,2,3).
        // LEAST() is MySQL; SQLite (the test database) spells it MIN().
        $least   = DB::connection()->getDriverName() === 'sqlite' ? 'MIN' : 'LEAST';
        $pdCase  = "CASE ifrs9stage_post_qualitative WHEN 1 THEN ? WHEN 2 THEN ? WHEN 3 THEN ? ELSE 1 END";
        $lgCase  = "CASE ifrs9stage_post_qualitative WHEN 1 THEN ? WHEN 2 THEN ? WHEN 3 THEN ? ELSE 0 END";
        $baseEcl = self::EAD . ' * ' . self::PD . ' * ' . self::LGD;
        $strEcl  = self::EAD
            . " * $least(1, " . self::PD . " * ($pdCase))"
            . " * $least(1, " . self::LGD . " + ($lgCase))";

        // Binding order: stress PD case (3), stress LGD case (3).
        $b = [$pd[1], $pd[2], $pd[3], $lg[1], $lg[2], $lg[3]];

        $scope = function ($q) use ($period, $portfolioId) {
            $q->where('reporting_period', $period);
            if (! empty($portfolioId)) {
                $q->where('loan_portfolio_id', $portfolioId);
            }
            return $q;
        };

        $byStage = $scope(DB::table('loan_books'))
            ->whereIn('ifrs9stage_post_qualitative', [1, 2, 3])
            ->groupBy('ifrs9stage_post_qualitative')
            ->orderBy('ifrs9stage_post_qualitative')
            ->selectRaw(
                "ifrs9stage_post_qualitative AS stage,
                 COUNT(*) AS accounts,
                 SUM(" . self::EAD . ") AS exposure,
                 SUM($baseEcl) AS base_ecl,
                 SUM($strEcl) AS stress_ecl,
                 AVG(" . self::PD . ") AS avg_pd,
                 AVG(" . self::LGD . ") AS avg_lgd",
                $b
            )->get();

        $byPortfolio = $scope(DB::table('loan_books as lb'))
            ->leftJoin('loan_portfolios as p', 'p.id', 'lb.loan_portfolio_id')
            ->whereIn('ifrs9stage_post_qualitative', [1, 2, 3])
            ->groupBy('p.name')
            ->selectRaw(
                "COALESCE(p.name,'Unmapped') AS portfolio,
                 COUNT(*) AS accounts,
                 SUM(" . self::EAD . ") AS exposure,
                 SUM($baseEcl) AS base_ecl,
                 SUM($strEcl) AS stress_ecl",
                $b
            )->get()
            ->sortByDesc('stress_ecl')->values();

        $totBase   = (float) $byStage->sum('base_ecl');
        $totStress = (float) $byStage->sum('stress_ecl');

        return [
            'period'           => $period,
            'total_base_ecl'   => $totBase,
            'total_stress_ecl' => $totStress,
            'delta'            => $totStress - $totBase,
            'delta_pct'        => $totBase > 0 ? ($totStress - $totBase) / $totBase : 0,

new='''    public function execute(string $period, ?int $portfolioId, array $pd, array $lg): array
    {
        /*
        | On the ECL basis (system audit of 9 October 2026, H5 and the step-5
        | reconciliation): each loan's booked allowance (ecl_value, whichever
        | engine wrote it) scaled by the ratio of the stressed stage PD to the
        | booked stage PD and of the stressed LGD to the held LGD, by the stage
        | the ECL was measured on. The base case (multipliers 1, add-ons 0)
        | therefore equals the allowance to the kwacha; a loan with no booked
        | ECL is measured directly. Before, the stress recomputed 12-month PD x
        | LGD x EAD by the DPD-only stage and never agreed with the allowance.
        */
        $q = DB::table('loan_books')->where('reporting_period', $period);
        if (! empty($portfolioId)) {
            $q->where('loan_portfolio_id', $portfolioId);
        }
        $loans = $q->leftJoin('loan_portfolios as p', 'p.id', '=', 'loan_books.loan_portfolio_id')
            ->get(['loan_books.*', DB::raw("COALESCE(p.name, 'Unmapped') AS portfolio_name")]);

        $stagePd = function (string $stage, float $pd12, $tenor): float {
            $pd12 = max(0.0, min(1.0, $pd12));
            $months = $tenor === null || (float) $tenor < 1 ? 12.0 : (float) $tenor;
            return match ($stage) {
                '3' => 1.0,
                '2' => 1 - pow(1 - $pd12, $months / 12),
                default => 1 - pow(1 - $pd12, min(12.0, $months) / 12),
            };
        };

        $byStage = []; $byPortfolio = [];
        foreach ($loans as $l) {
            $stage = (string) ($l->ifrs9stage_post_qualitative ?? $l->calculated_ifrs9_stage ?? $l->ifrs9stage_pre_qualitative ?? '');
            if (! in_array($stage, ['1', '2', '3'], true)) {
                continue;
            }
            $i = (int) $stage;
            $ead = (float) ($l->carrying_amount ?? 0) + (float) ($l->commitments ?? 0) * (float) ($l->facility_utilisation_rate ?? 1);
            $pd12 = (float) ($l->pd_post_fli ?? $l->pd_prefli ?? 0);
            $lgd = (float) ($l->lgd_value ?? 0);
            $basePd = $stagePd($stage, $pd12, $l->remaining_tenor ?? null);
            $stressPd = $stagePd($stage, min(1.0, $pd12 * (float) ($pd[$i] ?? 1)), $l->remaining_tenor ?? null);
            $stressLgd = min(1.0, $lgd + (float) ($lg[$i] ?? 0));
            if ($l->ecl_value !== null && $basePd > 0 && $lgd > 0) {
                $base = (float) $l->ecl_value;
                $stress = $base * ($stressPd / $basePd) * ($stressLgd / $lgd);
            } else {
                $base = $ead * $basePd * $lgd;
                $stress = $ead * $stressPd * $stressLgd;
            }
            foreach ([['byStage', $stage], ['byPortfolio', (string) $l->portfolio_name]] as [$bucket, $key]) {
                $$bucket[$key] = $$bucket[$key] ?? ['accounts' => 0, 'exposure' => 0.0, 'base_ecl' => 0.0, 'stress_ecl' => 0.0, 'pd_sum' => 0.0, 'lgd_sum' => 0.0];
                $$bucket[$key]['accounts']++; $$bucket[$key]['exposure'] += $ead; $$bucket[$key]['base_ecl'] += $base; $$bucket[$key]['stress_ecl'] += $stress;
                $$bucket[$key]['pd_sum'] += $pd12; $$bucket[$key]['lgd_sum'] += $lgd;
            }
        }
        ksort($byStage);
        $rows = fn (array $groups, string $keyName) => collect($groups)->map(fn ($g, $k) => (object) [
            $keyName => $keyName === 'stage' ? (int) $k : $k, 'accounts' => $g['accounts'], 'exposure' => round($g['exposure'], 2),
            'base_ecl' => round($g['base_ecl'], 2), 'stress_ecl' => round($g['stress_ecl'], 2),
            'avg_pd' => $g['accounts'] ? $g['pd_sum'] / $g['accounts'] : 0, 'avg_lgd' => $g['accounts'] ? $g['lgd_sum'] / $g['accounts'] : 0,
        ])->values();
        $byStage = $rows($byStage, 'stage');
        $byPortfolio = $rows($byPortfolio, 'portfolio')->sortByDesc('stress_ecl')->values();

        $totBase   = (float) $byStage->sum('base_ecl');
        $totStress = (float) $byStage->sum('stress_ecl');

        return [
            'period'           => $period,
            'total_base_ecl'   => $totBase,
            'total_stress_ecl' => $totStress,
            'delta'            => $totStress - $totBase,
            'delta_pct'        => $totBase > 0 ? ($totStress - $totBase) / $totBase : 0,

    }

Tranches in the EIR vector; a short-window PD annualised; reports and stress by the measured stage; gross carrying in the note (audit H2, H8, H5, H6)

H2: a facility drawn in tranches was solved on the whole drawn amount at origination against a schedule that repays it all, so its EIR sat far above the contractual rate. The tranche register is now built from the ledger's type-301 postings (P3_12 is the plan, landed for reference; the postings are what was paid): 215 drawdowns on 131 facilities, 32 of them in more than one tranche. The EIR inputs take the money out at origination as the tranche(s) paid by then and every later tranche at its own date as a DISBURSEMENT flow, the one negative row the solver accepts; a two-tranche test solves to the contractual rate.

H8: a default rate measured over a window shorter than twelve months was written as a twelve-month PD; it is annualised, 1 - (1 - p)^(12/months), and the window is recorded.

H5: every report, the FS note, the ECL aggregate and the stress test split by ifrs9stage_pre_qualitative (the DPD-only stage) while the ECL was measured on the post-qualitative stage; a loan the instalment trigger moved to Stage 3 showed in Stage 1 with a PD of 1. They read the measured stage now.

H6: the FS note headed the EAD "Gross Carrying (EAD)" and netted the allowance from it; it carries the gross carrying amount, the EAD beside it, and the net from the gross.

The stress test is on the ECL basis like the sensitivity: each loan's booked allowance scaled by the stressed stage-PD and LGD ratios, so the base scenario equals the allowance to the kwacha (9,509,808,295 on the clean install; it had been 8.51bn beside a 9.51bn allowance).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log -1 --format='%h %s'

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-09 00:13:28 UTC)

All seven doable audit steps are done, proven on a clean install, committed and pushed (`d58a8b0` … `afb0efe`; `master` fast-forwarded). The audit and the After Build Report are updated and re-rendered to OneDrive.

**What changed, step by step**

1. **Gate** — one `RequireLogin` middleware: every web route needs a login; legacy financial modules need `loans`/`reports.ifrs9`/`settings`; API behind `auth:sanctum`, dead routes removed; the SQL interpolation bound; a test walks every GET route as a guest. (Also found a controller naming an unregistered `2fa` middleware that 500'd.)
2. **ECL on the IFRS 9 basis** — Stage 2 on the lifetime PD, `remaining_tenor` in months everywhere (`POWER` registered for sqlite so tests run the real SQL), Stage 3 loss at the reporting date with recoveries PV'd from their own dates, LGD workout with cure/recovery exclusive, write-offs as write-offs, discounted.
3. **Revenue** — Stage 3 nets the prior month's `ecl_value`; the bootstrap now runs PD/LGD/ECL for every month before revenue (25 of 26); cash falls back to the schedule only outside the feed's coverage (3 of 483 months, was most of Stage 3).
4. **300/401** out of cash as `Write-off` / `Settlement in kind` derecognition; ties re-proved 9/9. (401 sat on GL 3065 and never reached cash in practice.)
5. **Governance of the chain** — bootstrap approves no fit (overlay zero), reviews no fees; one scenario weighting from the set written on the loan; sensitivity reconciles to the booked allowance exactly.
6. **Locks and rules** — `ReportingPeriodLock::assertOpen` in every engine; thresholds at the period end, no silent 31/181 or 4; admin override is a governed setting, default "Not allowed" (49 settings).
7. **Tranches, PD, reports** — tranche register built from the ledger's 301 postings (32 multi-tranche facilities now solve with each tranche at its date); short-window PD annualised; every report, the FS note, the ECL aggregate and stress on the measured (post) stage; FS note shows gross carrying, EAD and net separately; stress base equals the allowance.

**Clean install at August 2026 now:** ECL **9.51bn** (S1 1.64 / S2 3.40 / S3 5.18), sensitivity base = allowance and weighted 9.88bn, stress severe 11.51bn, Stage 3 interest on net (1.00bn netted on the nine locked Stage 3 contracts), 27 locked EIRs, golden 9/9, ~120 s. Engagement suites: 331 passed, 0 failed.

**Two things worth your eye:** Mphunzitsi's EIR solves at 49% against a 28.6% contractual rate on four tranches — the same account whose sanction (1,047m vs 1,560m) the letters review flagged; and the fee rulebook approval now matters more, because with fees financed into principal every loan's initial net investment waits on it.

Left: audit step 8 (the spec gaps that mostly need MAIIC's decisions) and step 9 hygiene.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-09 05:41:17 UTC)

Step 8 is the group of findings I labelled **Medium** — things where the system is *incomplete against the specification* rather than *wrong in a number*. Nothing in step 8 changes the 9.51bn; each one is a control, a screen or a data path the spec asked for that isn't there yet. Think of them in four families.

**Family 1 — Doors the data should come through, but doesn't (M1, M2)**

The spec's rule is that everything enters the system through one landing zone with gates: hashes, counts, dates, keys, and the raw rows kept even when a load is refused. Two things slip past that door today.

- *M1, trial balances.* The TB is imported directly into `gl_trial_balance_lines` by its own importer — no hash, no load row, no quarantine. If someone sends a different TB file next quarter, the system can't tell you which one produced the December tie. Also GL_02 (the GL master) is landed but the reconciliation never reads it.
- *M2, the gates themselves.* The gate checks file hashes, counts and key uniqueness, but not the four things that catch bad data: every ledger account exists in the master; the balance history ties to the ledger's running balance; every in-scope account has a month-end row; numerics parse. It also accepts dates in whatever format the manifest declares (the committed pack is m/d/yyyy, against decision D23), records the query version but doesn't validate it, and a quarantined load keeps no rows to inspect.

Teaching point: the golden ties pass *because the data happens to be clean*. The gates are what make that true on the hundredth pack, not just the first.

**Family 2 — Governance the spec requires that has no home (M3, M4, M5, M12)**

The spec wants every judgement to have an owner, evidence, two approvals and an expiry.

- *M3, the overlay register.* When no regression fit is approved, the route uses a "manual overlay" — but there's no register for one: no scope, reason, evidence, owner, expiry, two approvals, or its own ECL line. The route just reads whatever the legacy `fli_adj` row says. Right now the overlay is zero, so nothing is wrong; the day Dr Thom wants to apply a 5% overlay for a drought, there's nowhere to record why.
- *M4, the overlay-lock tie.* Spec 15.7: a scenario set can't be locked while an unapproved overlay exists. The code has an empty `if` block where that check should be.
- *M5, the set editor.* The Scenario Sets screen can seed the fixed first set and approve/lock it, but can't change a weight, add a scenario or edit a shock. The one decision the spec reserves for the CFO — "the weights are his to set" — has no screen.
- *M12, decorative settings.* Fourteen of the 49 governed settings are read by nothing but the Governance Centre. They're honest placeholders for phases 5–8, but two are claimed built and aren't wired: `fli_expected_sign_test` ("Advisory" has no effect) and `macro_source_precedence` (the rule is hard-coded). And the FLI engines read a second parameter store with different defaults that a direct write would bypass.

**Family 3 — Engine behaviours the spec describes that are simplified (M6, M7, M10, M11, M13)**

- *M6, two regression chains.* The new chain (univariate, maker-checker, lineage) and the legacy screen (one-click approval, no test, no second person) both exist; the menu's "Regression Analysis" still points at the old one. Retire or re-point.
- *M7, take-on recompute.* The `takeon_history_basis` option "Recompute from origination" writes a label and nothing else — no EIR solved from the workbook schedule. Harmless today (no take-on fees exist); wrong the day Tamanda returns the fee template.
- *M10, PD by pre-stage.* The transition matrix is measured pre-qualitative to pre-qualitative, so a loan the four-instalment trigger moved to Stage 3 isn't a "default" in the PD's denominator, and loans leaving the book count as "Paid" (non-default) even when written off.
- *M11, no cure period.* Stage is recomputed from today's DPD only; a loan 95 days overdue last month and 85 today drops straight back to Stage 2. IFRS 9 practice (and the directive's s.15) expects a probation period.
- *M13, as-at date.* Download is CSV only (spec: Excel and PDF); the part-month accrual compounds the EIR rather than using the section-3 simple ACT/365 convention; the take-on basis isn't read.

**Family 4 — Things waiting on MAIIC or simply unbuilt (M14, M16, M18)**

- *M14, zip extraction* relies on PHP's internal `..` stripping with no explicit check. Small, cheap.
- *M16, screens and names.* Correlation Finder and the Auditor Pack are CLI-only; `macro.view/manage` permissions don't exist; two help chapters keep the old group names.
- *M18, Mega Farm section 16.* Beyond staging and PD, nothing: the 15% interest split, the maize repayment and buyer receivable, the fund roll-forward, the Mega Farms report, seasonal segmentation. All of it hinges on D30, which the audit says the current service misreads — so this waits for Dr Thom's confirmation before a line is written.

**How I'd sequence it**

| Order | Items | Why first | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | M4, M14, M16 (perms, menu) | Each is an hour and closes a control gap | 1 day |
| 2 | M2, M1 | The gates protect every future pack; do before the first live feed | 3–4 days |
| 3 | M3, M5 | Register and editor: needed the first time Dr Thom wants to exercise judgement | 3–4 days |
| 4 | M10, M11, M6 | Engine refinements; M11 needs a governed cure period (a decision) | 3 days |
| 5 | M7, M13, M12 | Once fees/take-on data arrive; the decorative settings as their phases come | 2–3 days |
| 6 | M18 | After D30 | 1–2 weeks |

Roughly two to three weeks of build, but interleaved with MAIIC's decisions — the cure period, D30, the overlay policy, the scenario weights — which is why the audit put it after the engine corrections rather than before.

````
--==============================================================================
-- MAIIC E-Banker: FOLLOW-UP EXTRACTS, PACK 2  |  Dupleix Institute  |  8 October 2026
--==============================================================================
-- Eleven read-only queries, numbered in run order, each with the file name to
-- save it under. Nothing here writes to the database. Run RUN 0 once at the
-- start of the session; it lasts for the session only.
--
-- The files to send back:
--
--   SEPTEMBER MONTH-END (the first monthly pack; three files plus the TB)
--     M09_01_ledger_since_august.csv        ledger rows since our last load, August re-pulled
--     M09_02_balance_history_aug_sep.csv    month-end balance rows for 31 Aug and 30 Sep 2026
--     M09_03_loan_book_runs_sep.csv         the Loan Book Report run(s) for 30 Sep 2026
--     (from Finance, not a query)           Trial Balance_30 September 2026.xls
--
--   THE INTEREST ARITHMETIC AND THE COLLATERAL
--     P1_05b_interest_product.csv           the balance-times-days behind every posting, if history is kept
--     P2_11_security_details.csv            collateral per customer
--     P2_12_guarantors.csv                  guarantors per account
--     P2_13_los_requests.csv                origination requests mentioning our accounts (fees and rates at approval)
--
--   THE YEAR-END ADJUSTMENTS (sent on 8 Oct as its own note; repeated here)
--     GL_03_diffint_batch_legs.csv          both legs of the interest batches of 31 Dec 2025
--
--   THE MEGA FARM SCHEMES (96 to 103; about 7,000 accounts; same shape as the 7 Oct pack)
--     MF_01_account_master.csv
--     MF_02_loan_master.csv
--     MF_03_ledger_all.csv                  the largest file; expect several times the MAIIC ledger
--     MF_04_balance_history.csv
--     MF_05_loan_book_history.csv
--     MF_06_status_history.csv
--     MF_07_rate_setup.csv
--     MF_08_charges.csv
--==============================================================================

-- RUN 0  |  session settings  |  run once, first
-- Dates come out as 2026-09-30 00:00:00 and decimals with a point, so no file
-- can be misread. They apply to this SQL Developer session only and change
-- nothing in the database; closing the session puts the defaults back.
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_DATE_FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS';
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS = '.,';


--==============================================================================
-- SEPTEMBER 2026 MONTH-END: the first monthly pack
--==============================================================================
-- The three queries below are the monthly feed. They take only what is new
-- since the files of 7 October (by the table's own id), and re-pull August so
-- that a posting back-dated into August after 7 October is seen.

-- RUN 1 of 11  |  save as M09_01_ledger_since_august.csv
-- Our last loaded ledger id is 425764. Everything after it, plus every August
-- row, for the 18 MAIIC schemes.
SELECT cv.*
FROM   cumvouch cv
WHERE  cv.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                            WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND   (cv.cumvouch_det_id > 425764 OR cv.transaction_date >= DATE '2026-08-01')
ORDER  BY cv.new_ac_number, cv.transaction_date, cv.cumvouch_det_id;


-- RUN 2 of 11  |  save as M09_02_balance_history_aug_sep.csv
-- Month-end balance rows for 31 August and 30 September 2026 (August re-pulled).
SELECT b.*
FROM   account_balance b
WHERE  b.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND    b.transaction_date IN (DATE '2026-08-31', DATE '2026-09-30')
ORDER  BY b.new_ac_number, b.transaction_date, b.account_bal_mst_id;


-- RUN 3 of 11  |  save as M09_03_loan_book_runs_sep.csv
-- Every stored run of the Loan Book Report with an as-on date of 30 September
-- 2026, and any run with an id after 808196 (our last), whatever its date.
SELECT l.*
FROM   loan_book_details_all l
WHERE  l.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND   (l.asondate = DATE '2026-09-30' OR l.loan_book_det_id_a > 808196)
ORDER  BY l.new_ac_number, l.asondate, l.loan_book_det_id_a;


--==============================================================================
-- THE INTEREST ARITHMETIC AND THE COLLATERAL
--==============================================================================

-- RUN 4 of 11  |  save as P1_05b_interest_product.csv
-- INTEREST_SUMMARY (P1_05) turned out to hold the latest month only.
-- INTEREST_PRODUCT carries the balance-times-days (PRINCIPAL_PRODUCT), the
-- days, the rate and the amount per calculation. If it keeps history, it is
-- the exact arithmetic behind every interest posting.
SELECT p.*
FROM   interest_product p
WHERE  p.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
ORDER  BY p.new_ac_number, p.product_from_date, p.interest_mst_id;


-- RUN 5 of 11  |  save as P2_11_security_details.csv
-- Collateral held per customer: description, value, type, reference, active.
-- Joined through the customer id of our 184 accounts.
SELECT a.new_ac_number, a.customer_id, s.*
FROM   cust_security_details s
JOIN   acmaster a ON a.customer_id = s.customer_id
WHERE  a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145)
ORDER  BY a.new_ac_number, s.cust_sec_det_id;


-- RUN 6 of 11  |  save as P2_12_guarantors.csv
-- Guarantors per account.
SELECT g.*
FROM   guaranter_master g
WHERE  g.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
ORDER  BY g.new_ac_number, g.guaranter_srno;

FOLLOW-UP extracts for Barry - pack 2 - 8 Oct 2026 (.sql, .txt, .pdf)
1. Thank you, and where we are
The 7 October pack answered more than we asked. Every reconciliation we could run either ties to the cent
or has a named cause, the specification for the engine is written, and the data you sent is committed as the
bootstrap of the system so that any server can be built from it. This second pack has four groups. None is
urgent in the way the first was; the September month-end group is the one we would run first, because it is
the monthly routine from now on.
2. The September month-end pack (RUN 1 to 3)
From now on, each month-end needs three files from the database and the trial balance from Finance. The
queries take only what is new since 7 October, by each table's own id, and re-pull August so that a posting
back-dated into August after the 7th is seen. The ids in the queries (425764 for the ledger, 808196 for the
loan-book runs) are the last ones we hold; next month we will send the new ids. Finance's file is Trial
Balance_30 September 2026.xls, the same shape as the others.
File
What it is
M09_01_ledger_since_august.csv
Ledger rows after id 425764, plus every August row
M09_02_balance_history_aug_sep.csv
Month-end balance rows for 31 August and 30 September
M09_03_loan_book_runs_sep.csv
The Loan Book Report run(s) for 30 September, and any run with a
later id
Trial Balance_30 September 2026.xls
From Finance, not a query
3. The interest arithmetic and the collateral (RUN 4 to 7)
P1_05b, INTEREST_PRODUCT. The interest summary you sent twice (P1_05) holds the latest month only.
INTEREST_PRODUCT carries the balance-times-days, the days, the rate and the amount for each
calculation; if it keeps history, it is the exact arithmetic behind every interest posting since go-live and our
rebuild becomes an exact reproduction rather than a 99.9 percent one.
P2_11 and P2_12, collateral and guarantors. Nothing on security has been extracted yet; the collateral
screens in the system are fed by hand. CUST_SECURITY_DETAILS has 1,197 rows and GUARANTER_MASTER
3,368; the queries take those for our customers. They feed the loss-given-default side of the expected
credit loss.
P2_13, LOS_REQUEST_DETAILS. A long shot with a large prize. The origination system's request and
response payloads (202,184 rows) may carry the fees and the rate as captured at approval. If they do, part
of what we have asked Tamanda to type into the take-on workbook can come from the system instead.
The query searches the text of each payload for our account numbers, so it runs for a few minutes; that is
normal.

 * anything outside them is refused with a named reason rather than bent into
 * the nearest shape the code already had:
 *
 *  - Moratorium. E-Banker's Moratorium Type has exactly two options (LOS
 *    p.76, decision D4): "Principle Only", where the borrower pays interest
 *    but no principal and the balance does not grow, and "Both (Interest +
 *    Principle)", where nothing is paid, the interest is added to the balance
 *    each month (decision D10) and the instalment is then sized on the
 *    enlarged balance. No third shape exists in 33 months of loan books, so
 *    none is built. A moratorium with no type stated is refused: the two
 *    shapes give different cash flows and the engine does not guess.
 *    The moratorium runs from the first disbursement date (E-Banker p.31),
 *    which is `moratorium_from`, not from approval. `grace_period_months` is
 *    E-Banker's separate grace and is carried through untouched: it is never
 *    folded into the moratorium.

**Tool call: Bash**

````
description: Derive the moratorium type from the loan master's two numbers
--- command ---
cd /c/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9 && python - <<'EOF'
import io
p='app/Services/Ebanker/ContractInputsBuildService.php'; s=io.open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
old="""                'tenor_months' => $months, 'moratorium_months' => (int) $this->num($l['PMOROTORIUM_PERIOD'] ?? 0),"""
new="""                'tenor_months' => $months, 'moratorium_months' => (int) $this->num($l['PMOROTORIUM_PERIOD'] ?? 0),
                // The loan master states the moratorium in two numbers, not a word:
                // PMOROTORIUM_PERIOD (months without principal) and IMOROTORIUM_PERIOD
                // (months without interest). Interest deferred as well as principal is
                // E-Banker's "Both (Interest + Principle)", capitalising; principal
                // deferred and interest paid is "Principle Only". 51 contracts had
                // been refused a schedule for "a moratorium with no type stated"
                // (system audit of 9 October 2026, section 5); the three signed offer
                // letters that state a moratorium all read "principal and interest",
                // which is what their P and I months say here. Barry asked to confirm.
                'moratorium_type' => (int) $this->num($l['PMOROTORIUM_PERIOD'] ?? 0) <= 0 ? null
                    : ((int) $this->num($l['IMOROTORIUM_PERIOD'] ?? 0) > 0 ? 'Both (Interest + Principle)' : 'Principle Only'),
                'interest_moratorium_months' => (int) $this->num($l['IMOROTORIUM_PERIOD'] ?? 0),"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1); io.open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8',newline='\n').write(s); print('ok')
EOF

description: Test and commit the moratorium derivation
--- command ---
cd /c/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9 && php artisan test tests/Feature/Ebanker tests/Feature/Eir/ContractMasterImportServiceTest.php 2>&1 | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -E "⨯|Tests:" | head -3; git add app/Services/Ebanker/ContractInputsBuildService.php && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
The moratorium type is read from the loan master's two numbers; 48 more schedules generate

The schedule generator refused 51 contracts for "a moratorium is stated but its type is not". The loan master never states the type as a word: it carries PMOROTORIUM_PERIOD (months without principal) and IMOROTORIUM_PERIOD (months without interest). Interest deferred as well as principal is E-Banker's "Both (Interest + Principle)", capitalising; principal deferred with interest paid is "Principle Only". The build now derives the type from the pair (44 Both, 27 Principle Only on the committed pack); the three signed offer letters that state a moratorium all read "principal and interest", which is what their numbers say. On the clean install 95 of 144 contracts now generate a schedule (47 before); the remaining 49 are 38 undrawn facilities, 8 part-drawn awaiting the interest-basis decision and 2 with no rate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
