--- content ---
--==============================================================================
-- MAIIC E-Banker: FOLLOW-UP EXTRACTS, PACK 3  |  Dupleix Institute  |  9 October 2026
--==============================================================================
-- Read-only queries, numbered in run order, each with the file name to save
-- it under. Nothing here writes to the database. Run RUN 0 once at the start
-- of the session, before anything else; it lasts for the session only.
--
-- Three groups:
--
--   A. STILL OPEN FROM PACK 2 (8 October)
--     M09_03_loan_book_runs_sep.csv         the Loan Book Report run(s) for 30 Sep 2026
--     P2_13_los_requests.csv                RE-RUN: the payloads rendered as text this time
--     MF_01 .. MF_08                         the eight Mega Farm files (schemes 96 to 103)
--     (from Finance, not a query)           Trial Balance_30 September 2026.xls
--
--   B. NEW THIS WEEK, FROM THE BUILD
--     SM_01_scheme_master.csv               the 26 schemes' settings (moratorium, interest basis)
--     CT_01_table_counts.csv                row counts of the reschedule, write-off and charges tables
--     CH_01_charges_term_loans.csv          charges on the term-loan schemes 140 to 145
--     RS_01_reschedules.csv  WO_01_writeoffs.csv   only if CT_01 shows rows
--
--   C. THE OCTOBER MONTH-END (to run on 1 November; the ids are current)
--     M10_01_ledger_since_september.csv, M10_02_balance_history_sep_oct.csv, M10_03_loan_book_runs_oct.csv
--==============================================================================

-- RUN 0  |  session settings  |  run once, first
-- The 7 and 8 October files came out with dates as m/d/yyyy because these two
-- lines were not run first. The system now records on every load whether its
-- dates were ISO; from this pack on it should say yes. They apply to this SQL
-- Developer session only and change nothing in the database.
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_DATE_FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS';
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS = '.,';

-- EXPORT SETTINGS (SQL Developer, Export Data): format CSV, header yes,
-- delimiter comma, string enclosure double quotes, encoding UTF-8, no
-- thousand separators (RUN 0 covers the numbers), left-aligned dates as RUN 0
-- formats them. One file per query, named as shown.


--==============================================================================
-- A. STILL OPEN FROM PACK 2
--==============================================================================

-- RUN 1  |  save as M09_03_loan_book_runs_sep.csv
-- Every stored run of the Loan Book Report with an as-on date of 30 September
-- 2026, and any run with an id after 808196 (our last), whatever its date.
-- This is the one September file we do not yet hold; without it the month
-- cannot be built by method A and compared with method B.
SELECT l.*
FROM   loan_book_details_all l
WHERE  l.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND   (l.asondate = DATE '2026-09-30' OR l.loan_book_det_id_a > 808196)
ORDER  BY l.new_ac_number, l.asondate, l.loan_book_det_id_a;


-- RUN 2  |  save as P2_13_los_requests.csv   (RE-RUN)
-- The 8 October file carried the literal text "CLOB" in REQUEST_STRING and
-- RESPONCE_STRING because SQL Developer does not export a CLOB as text by
-- default. This version renders the first 4,000 characters of each payload
-- as text (two columns, so a payload longer than 4,000 characters is still
-- seen in full). The join is a text search, so a few minutes is normal.
SELECT a.new_ac_number,
       r.los_req_id, r.transaction_date,
       DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(r.request_string, 4000, 1)     AS request_text_1,
       DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(r.request_string, 4000, 4001)  AS request_text_2,
       DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(r.responce_string, 4000, 1)    AS response_text_1,
       DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(r.responce_string, 4000, 4001) AS response_text_2
FROM   los_request_details r
JOIN   acmaster a ON INSTR(r.request_string, a.new_ac_number) > 0
                  OR INSTR(r.responce_string, a.new_ac_number) > 0
WHERE  a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145)
ORDER  BY a.new_ac_number, r.transaction_date, r.los_req_id;


-- RUN 3  |  save as MF_01_account_master.csv and MF_02_loan_master.csv (two queries)
-- The Mega Farm schemes 96 to 103, about 7,000 accounts, same shape as the
-- 7 October pack. Unchanged from pack 2.
SELECT a.*
FROM   acmaster a
WHERE  a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103)
ORDER  BY a.scheme_mst_id, a.new_ac_number;

SELECT lm.*
FROM   acloanmaster lm
WHERE  lm.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
ORDER  BY lm.new_ac_number;


-- RUN 4  |  save as MF_03_ledger_all.csv, MF_04_balance_history.csv, MF_05_loan_book_history.csv (three queries)
-- MF_03 is the largest file of the pack: expect several times the MAIIC ledger.
SELECT cv.*
FROM   cumvouch cv
WHERE  cv.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
ORDER  BY cv.new_ac_number, cv.transaction_date, cv.cumvouch_det_id;

SELECT b.*
FROM   account_balance b
WHERE  b.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
AND    b.transaction_date = LAST_DAY(b.transaction_date)
ORDER  BY b.new_ac_number, b.transaction_date;

SELECT l.*
FROM   loan_book_details_all l
WHERE  l.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
ORDER  BY l.new_ac_number, l.asondate, l.loan_book_det_id_a;


-- RUN 5  |  save as MF_06_status_history.csv, MF_07_rate_setup.csv, MF_08_charges.csv (three queries)
SELECT h.*
FROM   account_status_history h
WHERE  h.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
ORDER  BY h.new_ac_number, h.status_eff_date, h.ac_status_mst_id;

SELECT r.*
FROM   interest_slab_details r
WHERE  r.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
ORDER  BY r.new_ac_number, r.applicable_from_date, r.interest_rate_det_id;

SELECT c.*
FROM   los_disb_charges_post c
WHERE  c.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
ORDER  BY c.new_ac_number, c.lo_disb_charg_det_id;


--==============================================================================
-- B. NEW THIS WEEK, FROM THE BUILD
--==============================================================================

-- RUN 6  |  save as SM_01_scheme_master.csv
-- The scheme settings for the 18 MAIIC schemes and the 8 Mega Farm schemes:
-- the moratorium period and unit, whether interest is charged on the
-- sanctioned or the disbursed amount (LOANINT_SANCWISE_BALWISE), the interest
-- calculation and payment frequencies, the product frequency. Two things in
-- the build wait on this: eight part-drawn facilities whose interest basis
-- neither the contract nor the scheme has told us yet, and a check of our
-- reading of the loan master's moratorium fields (see the note).
SELECT s.*
FROM   scheme_master s
WHERE  s.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145,96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103)
ORDER  BY s.scheme_mst_id;


-- RUN 7  |  save as CT_01_table_counts.csv
-- Before we ask for any of these tables: how many rows each holds, in all
-- and for our schemes. The data dictionary of 6 October showed
-- LOAN_RESCHEDULE_DETAILS and LOAN_WRITEOFF_TRANS empty; if that is right the
-- restructure history is still the vendor's Reschedule Report, and the
-- write-offs are only the two type-300 postings in the ledger. If any count
-- is above zero, RUN 9 and RUN 10 extract them.
SELECT 'LOAN_RESCHEDULE_DETAILS' AS table_name, COUNT(*) AS all_rows,
       SUM(CASE WHEN new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145)) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS our_rows
FROM   loan_reschedule_details
UNION ALL
SELECT 'T_RESCHEDULE', COUNT(*), NULL FROM t_reschedule
UNION ALL
SELECT 'LOAN_WRITEOFF_MASTER', COUNT(*),
       SUM(CASE WHEN new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145)) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
FROM   loan_writeoff_master
UNION ALL
SELECT 'LOAN_WRITEOFF_TRANS', COUNT(*), NULL FROM loan_writeoff_trans
UNION ALL
SELECT 'CHARGES_POSTING_HISTORY', COUNT(*), NULL FROM charges_posting_history
UNION ALL
SELECT 'CHARGES_POSTING_HISALL', COUNT(*), NULL FROM charges_posting_hisall
UNION ALL
SELECT 'DISBURSE_CHARGES_DETAILS', COUNT(*), NULL FROM disburse_charges_details
UNION ALL
SELECT 'LOS_DISB_CHARGES_POST', COUNT(*),
       SUM(CASE WHEN new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (140,141,142,143,144,145)) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
FROM   los_disb_charges_post;
-- If a table in this list does not exist under this name, drop that UNION
-- branch and tell us the name it goes by.


-- RUN 8  |  save as CH_01_charges_term_loans.csv
-- The charges table we hold (P2_07, LOS_DISB_CHARGES_POST) carries fees for
-- the MAIIC Industrial and FInES loans but none for the term-loan schemes
-- 140 to 145, although the signed offer letters show arrangement and legal
-- fees on every one of them (Malawi Police SACCO 90,000,000 and 48,771,287,
-- for example, deducted in January 2026). Either they are posted elsewhere
-- or through the ledger alone. This pulls every charges-type row we can find
-- for those six schemes from the three charges tables; where a table has no
-- NEW_AC_NUMBER column, tell us its key and we will adjust.
SELECT 'CHARGES_POSTING_HISTORY' AS source, c.*
FROM   charges_posting_history c
WHERE  c.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (140,141,142,143,144,145))
ORDER  BY c.new_ac_number;

SELECT 'DISBURSE_CHARGES_DETAILS' AS source, d.*
FROM   disburse_charges_details d
WHERE  d.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (140,141,142,143,144,145))
ORDER  BY d.new_ac_number;


-- RUN 9  |  save as RS_01_reschedules.csv   (only if CT_01 shows rows for our schemes)
SELECT r.*
FROM   loan_reschedule_details r
WHERE  r.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
ORDER  BY r.new_ac_number, r.transaction_date, r.loan_resch_det_id;


-- RUN 10  |  save as WO_01_writeoffs.csv   (only if CT_01 shows rows for our schemes)
SELECT w.*
FROM   loan_writeoff_master w
WHERE  w.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
ORDER  BY w.new_ac_number;


--==============================================================================
-- C. THE OCTOBER MONTH-END  (run on or after 1 November 2026)
--==============================================================================
-- The monthly routine. The ids below are the last ones we hold after landing
-- the 8 October files: ledger 439206, balance history 363004, loan-book runs
-- 808196 (or the id of the September run once RUN 1 arrives). Each query
-- takes what is new since then and re-pulls September, so a posting
-- back-dated into September after this pack is seen.

-- RUN 11  |  save as M10_01_ledger_since_september.csv
SELECT cv.*
FROM   cumvouch cv
WHERE  cv.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                            WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND   (cv.cumvouch_det_id > 439206 OR cv.transaction_date >= DATE '2026-09-01')
ORDER  BY cv.new_ac_number, cv.transaction_date, cv.cumvouch_det_id;

-- RUN 12  |  save as M10_02_balance_history_sep_oct.csv
SELECT b.*
FROM   account_balance b
WHERE  b.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND    b.transaction_date IN (DATE '2026-09-30', DATE '2026-10-31')
ORDER  BY b.new_ac_number, b.transaction_date, b.account_bal_mst_id;

-- RUN 13  |  save as M10_03_loan_book_runs_oct.csv
SELECT l.*
FROM   loan_book_details_all l
WHERE  l.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND   (l.asondate = DATE '2026-10-31' OR l.loan_book_det_id_a > 808196)
ORDER  BY l.new_ac_number, l.asondate, l.loan_book_det_id_a;

--==============================================================================
-- End of pack 3. Thank you, Barry.
--==============================================================================

````

--- content ---
---
kicker: MAIIC | E-BANKER EXTRACTS
title: Follow-up extracts, pack 3
subtitle: What the 8 October files did, what is still open from pack 2, three things to do differently on the re-run, and the new queries this week's build raised
date: 9 October 2026
prepared: A note for Barry Makumba, with Dr Thom and Tamanda copied, from Dupleix Institute. Goes with the file FOLLOW-UP extracts for Barry - pack 3 - 9 Oct 2026.sql
status: Thirteen read-only queries in three groups. Group A first; group C is the October month-end, to run on or after 1 November.
---

## 1. Thank you, and what the 8 October files did

Seven of pack 2's eleven files reached us on 8 October, and each one moved the build:

| File | What it answered |
|---|---|
| GL_03 (both legs of the 31 December batches) | Settled the year-end question: the 6 credits went through interest income 4215 and 4216 and the system now ties both legs to the cent in its golden checks. |
| M09_01 (ledger since August) and M09_02 (balances) | Landed as the first monthly pack. The feed's gates pass them; the ledger now runs to 30 September. |
| P1_05b (INTEREST_PRODUCT) | Keeps history (October 2024 to September 2026) and its monthly totals equal the ledger's interest postings on 1,763 of 1,818 account-months. Its "product" column holds the interest, not balance-times-days, and the days column is zero, so it confirms the postings rather than explaining them; useful as it is. |
| P2_11 (security) and P2_12 (guarantors) | Loaded; the collateral register now shows 185 security rows and feeds the RBM return's security line. |
| P2_13 (LOS requests) | Arrived with the word "CLOB" where the payload text should be (see section 3); kept for its keywords, re-run below. |

## 2. Still open from pack 2 (group A of the file)

| File | Why it matters now |
|---|---|
| **M09_03** the Loan Book Report run for 30 September | The one September file we do not hold. Without it September cannot be built by method A and compared with method B, which is the monthly control the specification sets. Query unchanged from pack 2 (RUN 1). |
| **P2_13** re-run | See section 3; RUN 2 renders the payloads as text. |
| **MF_01 to MF_08** the Mega Farm schemes 96 to 103 | The Mega Farm module exists and has run on a demonstration copy; it cannot run on the real book until these arrive. RUN 3 to 5, unchanged from pack 2. MF_03 (the ledger) will be the largest file of the pack. |
| **Trial Balance_30 September 2026.xls** | From Finance, not a query. The trial balances now land through the same door as the packs, with a hash on each file. |

## 3. Three things to do differently on the re-run

1. **Run RUN 0 first.** The two ALTER SESSION lines make dates come out as 2026-09-30 and decimals with a point. They were not run before the 7 and 8 October exports, so every date arrived as m/d/yyyy. The system coped (the manifest declares the format), but it now records on every load whether its dates were ISO, and from this pack on that should say yes. The lines last for the SQL Developer session only and change nothing in the database.
2. **P2_13: the payloads need rendering.** REQUEST_STRING and RESPONCE_STRING are CLOB columns, and SQL Developer exports a CLOB as the word "CLOB" unless told otherwise. RUN 2 wraps each in DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR, in two 4,000-character pieces, so the text itself comes out. This is the file that may carry the fees and the rate as captured at approval, which would spare Tamanda some typing.
3. **Export settings.** CSV, header row, comma delimiter, strings in double quotes, UTF-8, one file per query named as the file says. P2_06 (the PLR master) lost the date on PLR id 2 in its afternoon re-export on 7 October; we kept the morning one. If you re-export anything from pack 1, RUN 0 first and the same settings.

## 4. New this week, from the build (group B)

This week the engine was audited end to end and then corrected; the clean install now rebuilds itself from your files in about two and a half minutes and every reconciliation ties. Four things it turned up are yours.

**SM_01, the scheme master (RUN 6).** Two uses. First, eight part-drawn facilities (Lake Malawi Aquaculture is one: 1,055m approved, 297m drawn) cannot get a schedule because neither the contract nor the scheme has told the system whether interest runs on the sanctioned or the disbursed amount; LOANINT_SANCWISE_BALWISE on the scheme should say. Second, a check of our reading of the loan master: the schedule generator had refused 51 contracts for "a moratorium with no type stated". We found the type is not a word in E-Banker but two numbers, PMOROTORIUM_PERIOD (months without principal) and IMOROTORIUM_PERIOD (months without interest). We now read 3|3 as "Both (Interest + Principle)", capitalising, and 6|0 as "Principle Only", and 48 of the 51 generate. The three signed offer letters that state a moratorium (JVD, Lake Malawi, VNC) all say principal and interest, which is what their numbers say. **Please confirm that reading is right**, and whether MORT_PERIOD_SEP_INT (Y or blank) changes it.

**CT_01, row counts (RUN 7).** The data dictionary of 6 October showed LOAN_RESCHEDULE_DETAILS and LOAN_WRITEOFF_TRANS empty. If that is right, the restructure history stays with the vendor's Reschedule Report (still owed) and the write-offs are the two type-300 postings in the ledger (Micholess Creameries and Maluso Cooperative, 22.3m). If any count is above zero for our schemes, RUN 9 and RUN 10 extract them and we stop waiting on the vendor for that part.

**CH_01, charges on the term loans (RUN 8).** P2_07 carries fees for the Industrial and FInES loans and matches the signed letters to the kwacha (Ebenezer Midian: 9,000,000 arrangement, 3,090,000 legal, 2,810,900 levy and stamp duty). For the term-loan schemes 140 to 145 it carries nothing, yet every signed term-loan letter shows the same fees (Malawi Police SACCO 90,000,000 and 48,771,287, deducted in January 2026). Either they are posted in another charges table or through the ledger alone. RUN 8 looks in the two other charges tables; if neither has them, tell us and the fees will be keyed from the letters.

**Two corrections to the loan master, from the signed letters.** Not queries; the letters are in the Offer Letters folder.
- Mchinji Civil Servants SACCO, 000104460000070: the 2023 letter is a 100,000,000 facility disbursed in two tranches of 50,000,000. The master holds 50,000,000 as the sanction; the facility is 100,000,000.
- VNC Bricks and Construction, 000104430000054: the 2022 letter is 200,000,000. The master holds 20,000,000, a typing slip.

**Still open from earlier notes:** the meaning of status code H; the Zaithwa Farms balance rows from May 2025 (the one account the balance-history gate still flags, 34 month-ends); the vendor's Reschedule Report.

## 5. The October month-end (group C)

RUN 11 to 13 are the monthly routine for October, to run on or after 1 November. The ids in them are the last we hold after the 8 October files: ledger 439206, balance history 363004, loan-book runs 808196 (that one moves once M09_03 arrives). Each takes what is new since then and re-pulls September, so a posting back-dated into September after this pack is seen. The trial balance for October comes from Finance in the same way.

## 6. In one list

| Run | File | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | M09_03_loan_book_runs_sep.csv | open from pack 2 |
| 2 | P2_13_los_requests.csv | re-run, payloads as text |
| 3 to 5 | MF_01 to MF_08 | open from pack 2 |
| 6 | SM_01_scheme_master.csv | new |
| 7 | CT_01_table_counts.csv | new |
| 8 | CH_01_charges_term_loans.csv | new |
| 9, 10 | RS_01, WO_01 | only if CT_01 shows rows |
| 11 to 13 | M10_01 to M10_03 | 1 November |
| Finance | Trial Balance_30 September 2026.xls | open from pack 2 |

Thank you. Group A keeps the build moving this week; group B settles four questions the audit left; group C is the routine from now on.

Edward Mazibuko and Wadzanai Rombe, Dupleix Institute

--- content ---
"""Render a .sql run sheet to a monospace A4 PDF with a title band and page numbers."""
import sys, textwrap
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.lib.units import mm
from reportlab.lib import colors
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

src, out, title, sub = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
lines = open(src, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
W, H = A4
left, top, bottom = 16 * mm, H - 22 * mm, 16 * mm
font, size, lead = "Courier", 8.2, 10.2
maxw = 118  # characters per line at this size

def header(c, page):
    c.setFillColor(colors.HexColor("#0b2b1a")); c.rect(0, H - 14 * mm, W, 14 * mm, fill=1, stroke=0)
    c.setFillColor(colors.white); c.setFont("Helvetica-Bold", 10); c.drawString(left, H - 9 * mm, title)
    c.setFont("Helvetica", 7.5); c.drawRightString(W - left, H - 9 * mm, sub)
    c.setFillColor(colors.HexColor("#666666")); c.setFont("Helvetica", 7.5)
    c.drawString(left, 9 * mm, "Read-only queries. Run RUN 0 first. One CSV per query, named as shown.")
    c.drawRightString(W - left, 9 * mm, "Page %d" % page)
    c.setFillColor(colors.black); c.setFont(font, size)

c = canvas.Canvas(out, pagesize=A4); page = 1; header(c, page); y = top
for raw in lines:
    pieces = textwrap.wrap(raw, maxw, subsequent_indent="       ", drop_whitespace=False) or [""]
    for piece in pieces:
        if y < bottom + lead:
            c.showPage(); page += 1; header(c, page); y = top
        if raw.lstrip().startswith("-- RUN") or raw.startswith("--====") or raw.lstrip().startswith("-- "):
            c.setFillColor(colors.HexColor("#1f5f3f") if raw.lstrip().startswith("-- RUN") else colors.HexColor("#555555"))
            if raw.lstrip().startswith("-- RUN"): c.setFont("Courier-Bold", size)
        else:
            c.setFillColor(colors.black)
        c.drawString(left, y, piece); c.setFont(font, size); y -= lead
c.save(); print("written", out, "pages", page)

````

"""Draft .eml (X-Unsent, opens in Outlook as a draft) with two PDF attachments."""
import os, mimetypes
from email.message import EmailMessage
from email.utils import formatdate, make_msgid

folder = r"C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\Raw Query Scripts\Query Requests to MAIIC"
runsheet = os.path.join(folder, "FOLLOW-UP extracts for Barry - pack 3 - 9 Oct 2026.pdf")
note = os.path.join(folder, "Note to Barry - follow-up extracts pack 3 - 9 Oct 2026.pdf")
sql = os.path.join(folder, "FOLLOW-UP extracts for Barry - pack 3 - 9 Oct 2026.sql")

msg = EmailMessage()
msg["From"] = "Edward Mazibuko <edward@dupleixinstitute.com>"
msg["To"] = "Barry Makumba <bmakumba@maiic.mw>"
msg["Cc"] = ", ".join([
    "Thomson Kumwenda <tkumwenda@maiic.mw>",
    "Tamanda Sitimawina <tsitimawina@maiic.mw>",
    "Vanessa Magaleta <vmagaleta@maiic.mw>",
    "Kundai Muriwo <kundai@dupleixinstitute.com>",
    "Wadzanai Rombe <wadzanai@dupleixinstitute.com>",
])
msg["Subject"] = "MAIIC EIR: extracts pack 3 - the September loan-book run, the P2_13 re-run, the Mega Farm files, and four new queries"
msg["Date"] = formatdate(localtime=True)
msg["Message-ID"] = make_msgid(domain="dupleixinstitute.com")
msg["X-Unsent"] = "1"

text = """Dear Barry,

Thank you for the seven files of 8 October. GL_03 settled the year-end legs, the September ledger and balances landed as the first monthly pack, and the security and guarantor tables are loaded. Every one of them moved the build.

Attached are two PDFs:

1. FOLLOW-UP extracts for Barry - pack 3 (4 pages): the run sheet. Thirteen read-only queries in run order, each with the file name to save it under. The .sql is attached too, to paste from.
2. Note to Barry - pack 3: what each file is for, with Dr Thom and Tamanda copied.

Three things to do differently this time, in the order they matter:

- Run RUN 0 first, before any query. The two ALTER SESSION lines make dates come out as 2026-09-30 and decimals with a point. They were not run before the 7 and 8 October exports, so every date arrived as m/d/yyyy; the system coped, but it now records on every load whether the dates were ISO, and from this pack on that should say yes. They last for the session only and change nothing in the database.
- P2_13 needs re-running as RUN 2. The 8 October file carried the word "CLOB" where the payload text should be, because SQL Developer does not export a CLOB as text unless told to; RUN 2 renders the first 8,000 characters of each payload as text.
- Export as CSV with a header row, comma delimiter, strings in double quotes, UTF-8, one file per query named as the sheet says.

Group A is what is still open from pack 2 and keeps the build moving this week: M09_03, the Loan Book Report run for 30 September (the one September file we do not hold); the P2_13 re-run; and the eight Mega Farm files, MF_01 to MF_08, which the Mega Farm module is waiting on. The trial balance for 30 September comes from Tamanda in the usual way.

Group B is four short queries this week's build raised: the scheme master (the interest basis on part-drawn facilities, and a check of our reading of the moratorium fields, which the note explains); row counts of the reschedule, write-off and charges tables; and the charges on the term-loan schemes 140 to 145, which the signed offer letters show but P2_07 does not carry. Two corrections to the loan master from the signed letters are in the note as well (Mchinji SACCO 100,000,000; VNC Bricks 200,000,000).

Group C is the October month-end routine, to run on or after 1 November; the ids in it are current.

If any table in group B goes by a different name on your side, just tell us the name and we will adjust.

With thanks,

Edward Mazibuko
Director, Data Analytics
Dupleix Institute
"""
msg.set_content(text)

for path in [runsheet, note, sql]:
    ctype, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(path)
    maintype, subtype = (ctype or "application/octet-stream").split("/", 1)
    if path.endswith(".sql"):
        maintype, subtype = "text", "plain"
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        msg.add_attachment(fh.read(), maintype=maintype, subtype=subtype, filename=os.path.basename(path))

out = os.path.join(folder, "EMAIL - extracts pack 3 - 9 Oct 2026 (open in Outlook and send).eml")
with open(out, "wb") as fh:
    fh.write(bytes(msg))
print("written", out, os.path.getsize(out), "bytes")

````

file_path: C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\3. Project Execution\Database\README.md
--- content ---
# MAIIC IFRS 9 working databases, 9 October 2026

Two MySQL dumps of the working databases behind the system audit and the build of 8 and 9 October 2026, for colleagues who want to open the system as it stands without rebuilding it. **MAIIC client data: borrower names and balances. Treat as the production database is treated; do not copy outside OneDrive or the private repository.**

| File | Database | What it is | Size | SHA-256 (first 16) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `maiic_ifrs9_bootstrap_2026-10-09.sql.gz` | `maiic_ifrs9_bootstrap` | The clean install the audit and the After Build Report quote: built from nothing by `eir:bootstrap` at commit `72b495f`; 26 loan-book months to August 2026, every engine run, 9 of 9 golden ties, ECL 10.00bn | 7.7 MB | a1197d6797210198 |
| `maiic_ifrs9_demo_2026-10-09.sql.gz` | `maiic_ifrs9_demo` | The demonstration copy of 8 October, which also holds the November 2025 Mega Farm book (3,490 loans) | 7.9 MB | c909bbed562e76fa |

The code is on the private repository `MAICC-IFRS9`, branch `eir_revenue_recognition` (and `master`, kept level with it), head `72b495f` on 9 October 2026.

## Restore (XAMPP, Windows)

```
cd C:\xampp\htdocs\MAICC-IFRS9
git pull
C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe -uroot -e "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS maiic_ifrs9_bootstrap CHARACTER SET utf8mb4"
"C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\gzip.exe" -dc "<OneDrive>\3. Project Execution\Database\maiic_ifrs9_bootstrap_2026-10-09.sql.gz" | C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe -uroot maiic_ifrs9_bootstrap
copy .env.bootstrap.example .env.bootstrap
php artisan --env=bootstrap key:generate
php artisan --env=bootstrap migrate
npm install && npm run build
php artisan --env=bootstrap serve --port=8010
```

Then log in at http://127.0.0.1:8010 as `admin@localhost.com`; the password is the one in `MANUAL_SHOT_PASSWORD` of the shared `.env.bootstrap` (ask Wadzanai or Edward; it is not in the repository). The same steps with `demo` in place of `bootstrap` restore the demonstration copy. `.env.bootstrap` and `.env.demo` are git-ignored on purpose: each person keeps their own, from the `.example` files the repository carries.

## Or rebuild it from nothing (the proof the specification asks for)

The dump is a convenience. The system is built to rebuild this database from the committed client inputs under `docs/bootstrap` in about two and a half minutes:

```
php artisan --env=bootstrap eir:bootstrap --fresh --force-wipe --with-client-inputs --build --run-engines --verify
```

`--force-wipe` empties the named database first; never point it at `maiic_ifrs9` (the production copy). The run ends with the nine golden checks and the engine notes the After Build Report quotes.

## What to read

- `3. Project Execution/specs/MAIIC_System_Audit_2026-10-09.pdf`: the audit, its closures and the figures as restated.
- `3. Project Execution/specs/MAIIC_After_Build_Report_2026-10-08.pdf`: what was built against spec v4, section by section.
- `docs/manuals/installation` in the repository: the installation and data-loading manual.

````

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-09 08:40:39 UTC)

**What was asked, and what came back**

In pack 2 (and repeated in pack 3) the eight Mega Farm files were grouped into three runs to save Barry time, each run a block of two or three SELECT statements:

| Run | SELECTs in the block | Files asked for | What arrived |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9 (pack 2) / 3 (pack 3) | `acmaster` then `acloanmaster` | MF_01, MF_02 | one file, holding **only `acloanmaster`** = MF_02 |
| 10 / 4 | `cumvouch`, `account_balance`, `loan_book_details_all` | MF_03, MF_04, MF_05 | one file, holding **only `loan_book_details_all`** = MF_05 |
| 11 / 5 | `account_status_history`, `interest_slab_details`, `los_disb_charges_post` | MF_06, MF_07, MF_08 | one file, holding **only `los_disb_charges_post`** = MF_08 |

In every case the file contains the **last** SELECT of its block and none of the others. The file names ("MF_01_account_master.csv and MF_02_loan_master", with no extension) show what happened: Barry pasted the whole block, ran it, and exported the result grid once, naming the file after everything the block was meant to produce.

**Why SQL Developer does that**

When several statements are run together ("Run Script", F5), SQL Developer shows the output of each in turn, but the *Query Result* grid — the thing Export Data works on — holds only the last statement's rows. Exporting after the block gives one CSV of the last query. The first one or two queries' results were displayed in the script output pane and never saved. It's a tooling habit, not a mistake in the queries themselves: each SELECT is correct and the one that did come out is complete.

**What that leaves us with**

| Have | Rows | Use |
|---|---|---|
| MF_02 loan master | 6,973 accounts | sanction, tenor, rate, moratorium fields — but no account master to say which GL, scheme, customer or status each account carries |
| MF_05 loan-book runs | 34,540 rows, 160 accounts, GL 1050301 only, Dec 2024–Sep 2026 | the stored report for a small subset |
| MF_08 charges | 9,855 rows, 3,285 accounts | the fees at disbursement |

| Missing | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **MF_01 account master** | The spine. Without it we can't tie an account to its scheme (96–103), GL, customer or status; MF_02 can't be joined to anything. |
| **MF_03 ledger** | The record itself. Method B builds the monthly book from postings; without the ledger there is no Mega Farm book and no interest or cash history. Expected to be the largest file of the pack. |
| **MF_04 balance history** | The month-end balances the ledger is gated against (the balance-history tie). |
| MF_06 status history | Which accounts are live, written off, closed — the staging and LGD inputs. |
| MF_07 rate setup | The rate per account over time. |

So the module has the fee table and a sliver of the report, but not the two files it is built on. Nothing can run until MF_01 and MF_03 arrive; MF_04/06/07 complete it.

**The 160-account puzzle**

MF_05 is 34,540 rows for only 160 of the 6,973 accounts, and every row sits on GL 1050301. That means the Loan Book Report is only ever run for one of the Mega Farm GLs (1050301–1050307 are the programme's codes), or the other 6,800 accounts are on GLs the report excludes. Either way it's the account master that will say — another reason MF_01 comes first.

**The fix for Barry is procedural, not technical**

Re-issue the five missing ones as **one SELECT per run, one export per run, one file per run**, named as the run says — with a line in the sheet explaining why: "Run each query on its own and export its grid before running the next; a block of queries exports only the last one." RUN 0 first, as before. The three that did arrive needn't be re-run.

That's the change I'd make to pack 3 now, since the email is still a draft. Want me to do it?

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-09 09:04:16 UTC)

It's RUN 2 in the pack-3 run sheet:

`2. Documents from clients\Raw Query Scripts\Query Requests to MAIIC\FOLLOW-UP extracts for Barry - pack 3 - 9 Oct 2026.sql` (same content in the `.txt` and page 1–2 of the `.pdf`; a copy is in the repo at `docs/bootstrap/queries/Pack 3 - 9 Oct 2026.sql`).

This is the query:

```sql
-- RUN 2  |  save as P2_13_los_requests.csv   (RE-RUN)
SELECT a.new_ac_number,
       r.los_req_id, r.transaction_date,
       DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(r.request_string, 4000, 1)     AS request_text_1,
       DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(r.request_string, 4000, 4001)  AS request_text_2,
       DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(r.responce_string, 4000, 1)    AS response_text_1,
       DBMS_LOB.SUBSTR(r.responce_string, 4000, 4001) AS response_text_2
FROM   los_request_details r
JOIN   acmaster a ON INSTR(r.request_string, a.new_ac_number) > 0
                  OR INSTR(r.responce_string, a.new_ac_number) > 0
WHERE  a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145)
ORDER  BY a.new_ac_number, r.transaction_date, r.los_req_id;
```

The difference from the 8 October version is only the SELECT list: instead of `r.*`, the two CLOB columns are rendered as text in 4,000-character pieces (two each, so a payload up to 8,000 characters comes out whole). The join and filter are unchanged, so it takes the same few minutes.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-09 09:25:47 UTC)

Three ways, from quickest to most certain.

**1. In the session, before exporting anything — a one-line check**

Right after the two `ALTER SESSION` lines, run:

```sql
SELECT SYSDATE AS today_as_text, 1234567.89 AS a_number FROM dual;
```

If RUN 0 took, the grid shows `2026-10-09 11:14:05` and `1234567.89`. If it shows `09-OCT-26` (or `10/9/2026`) or `1234567,89`, the settings aren't in force — usually because the ALTER lines were run in a different worksheet/connection tab than the queries (each SQL Developer connection is its own session).

To see the settings themselves:

```sql
SELECT parameter, value FROM nls_session_parameters
WHERE parameter IN ('NLS_DATE_FORMAT','NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS');
```

Expected: `NLS_DATE_FORMAT = YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS`, `NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS = .,`.

I'd add both lines to the run sheet as "RUN 0a — check", so Barry sees the proof before running RUN 1.

**2. On the exported file — what to look at**

Open the CSV and look at any date column (e.g. `TRANSACTION_DATE`). RUN 0 applied gives `"2026-09-30 00:00:00"`; not applied gives `"9/30/2026"`. The first data row is enough.

One caveat that matters for SQL Developer specifically: the Export Data dialog has its own date format setting (Tools → Preferences → Database → NLS, and the export's "Format" options). The session NLS format governs how dates are *fetched*; the export can still re-format them. If the grid shows ISO but the file doesn't, the preference is overriding — set Preferences → Database → NLS → Date Format to `YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS` once, and it sticks for every export.

**3. On landing — the system now records it**

Since the audit's gates (M2), every load carries a `dates_iso` result on the Feed screen (Data Foundation → E-Banker Feed → the load's gates): PASS when every date column in every file is ISO, otherwise the files that aren't. The 7 and 8 October packs show 3 of 37 files ISO. The first pack after RUN 0 should show all of them.

So: Barry proves it with the `SELECT SYSDATE … FROM dual` line before exporting; we confirm it on the first row of the file and again on the Feed screen when it lands.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-09 09:40:58 UTC)

It's in the Preferences window, not in the Export dialog — and the Export dialog has no date option of its own, which is why it has to be set there.

**Where it is:** Tools → Preferences opens a window with a tree on the left. "Database" is one of the top-level nodes in that tree; click its ▸ to expand it and "NLS" is underneath. On that NLS page the first field is **Date Format**.

**If "Database" isn't visible in the tree**, use the search box at the top-left of the Preferences window: type `NLS` and the tree filters to Database → NLS. (The node is sometimes collapsed or scrolled past; in older versions it's named "Database: NLS Parameters" — same page.)

**If it's genuinely absent**, the tool isn't Oracle SQL Developer (some sites run queries through a vendor console or a different client). In that case the fallback is to make the query itself produce text dates, which no tool can re-format:

```sql
SELECT TO_CHAR(SYSDATE, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') AS today_as_text FROM dual;
```

For the `SELECT *` extracts that's impractical column by column, so the practical order is: (1) RUN 0 in the session, (2) the `SYSDATE` proof, (3) look at the first row of the first export — if it's still `m/d/yyyy`, tell us which tool and version is on screen (a screenshot of the Preferences window is enough) and I'll give the exact clicks for it.

START_MARK = "please build the code and do everything"
END_MARK = "__no_end_marker__"

def user_text(r):
    c = r.get("message", {}).get("content")
    if isinstance(c, str):
        return c
    return "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in c if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text")


start = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r.get("type") == "user" and START_MARK in user_text(r))
end = next((i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if i > start and r.get("type") == "user" and END_MARK in user_text(r)), len(rows))


def clean_user(t):
    t = re.sub(r"", "", t, flags=re.S)
    t = re.sub(r"<ide_opened_file>.*?</ide_opened_file>", "", t, flags=re.S)
    t = re.sub(r"<ide_selection>.*?</ide_selection>", "", t, flags=re.S)
    return t.strip()


def result_text(content):
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    out = []
    for b in content or []:
        if b.get("type") == "text":
            out.append(b.get("text", ""))
        elif b.get("type") == "image":
            out.append("[image output: not reproduced in this transcript]")
    return "\n".join(out)


def expand_persisted(t):
    """Where the harness stored a long output in a side file, inline the whole file."""
    m = re.search(r"Full output saved to: (\S.*?\.txt)", t)
    if m and os.path.exists(m.group(1)):
        return "[long output, reproduced in full from the saved file]\n" + open(m.group(1), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    return t
